content.p: If the Joint Authority grants an extension of an exploration licence under section 95 or 97, the Joint Authority must give the licence holder a written notice that informs the holder of:
the grant of extension; and
the period of the extension; and
if the extension is subject to conditions—the conditions.
If the Joint Authority refuses an application for a licence extension, the Joint Authority must give the licence holder a written notice that informs the holder of:
the refusal; and
the reasons for the refusal.

division.heading: Voluntary surrender of part of exploration licence area

section.heading: Voluntary surrender of blocks if discrete area remains

content.p: An exploration licence holder may surrender a block or some of the blocks covered by the licence if the remaining blocks in the licence area form a discrete area.
Note: See section 127 for the surrender of the whole licence.
A surrender under subsection (1) must:
be made in writing; and
identify the blocks surrendered; and
be given to the Designated Authority.
Note: The surrender takes effect when it is registered under section 337 (see subsection 337(5)).

section.heading: Voluntary surrender of blocks if up to 3 discrete areas remain

content.p: If:
an exploration licence holder wants to surrender some of the blocks covered by the licence; and
the blocks remaining in the licence area after the proposed surrender would form not more than 3 discrete areas;
the holder may apply to the Designated Authority for approval of the proposed surrender.
The application:
must be in writing; and
must include a surrender proposal that identifies the blocks in the licence area that the holder proposes to surrender; and
may include any other information that the holder thinks is relevant; and
must be lodged with the Designated Authority.

Subject to subsection (6), if the Designated Authority agrees with the surrender proposal the Designated Authority may approve the surrender of the blocks specified in the proposal by giving the holder written notice of the approval.
Note: The surrender takes effect when it is registered under section 337 (see subsection 337(5)).
If the Designated Authority does not agree with the surrender proposal, the Designated Authority may ask the holder to discuss the proposal.

Subject to subsection (6), if the Designated Authority and the holder agree, after discussions, on the blocks to be surrendered the Designated Authority may approve the surrender of the blocks agreed on by giving the holder written confirmation of the agreement.
Note: The surrender takes effect when it is registered under section 337 (see subsection 337(5)).
The Designated Authority may give approval under subsection (3) or (5) only with the approval of the Joint Authority.
Subsection (6) does not apply to a block in an external territory offshore area.
Note: The responsible Commonwealth Minister is both the Designated Authority (see subsection 29(3)) and the Joint Authority (see subsection 32(3)) for an external territory offshore area.
If, after discussions, the Designated Authority and the holder do not agree on the surrender proposal, no blocks are surrendered.

division.heading: Application for and grant of renewal of exploration licence

section.heading: Application for renewal of exploration licence

content.p: An exploration licence holder may apply to the Joint Authority to renew the licence.
Note 1: Part of the licence area must be surrendered on each renewal (see section 104).
Note 2: At each renewal, the licence conditions are reviewed (see section 118).

section.heading: When must an application to renew be made?

content.p: Subject to subsection (2), the application must be made at least 30 days before the day on which the licence is to expire.
Note: If an application for extension of a licence is made, the expiry of the licence is postponed (see section 91).
The Designated Authority may accept an application that is made later than 30 days before the day on which the licence is to expire if:
the application is made before the day on which the licence expires; and
the Designated Authority believes that there are reasonable grounds for accepting the application.

section.heading: How to apply for renewal

content.p: The application must:
be made in accordance with the approved form; and
be made in the approved manner; and
include details of:
the activities carried out by the applicant under the licence during its current term; and
the amount of money spent by the applicant in relation to the blocks covered by the licence during its current term; and
the activities that the applicant intends to carry out under the licence during the term applied for; and
the amount of money that the applicant intends to spend on those activities during the term applied for; and
specify the blocks that the applicant nominates for surrender in accordance with section 104.
Note: For paragraphs (a) and (b) see section 41.
The applicant may include in the application any other information that the applicant thinks is relevant.
The application must be lodged with the Designated Authority.

section.heading: Mandatory reduction of licence area on renewal of exploration licence

content.p: This section deals with the mandatory reduction of the licence area covered by an exploration licence when the licence is renewed.
Subject to paragraph (4)(b), on each surrender day of an exploration licence, the licence holder must surrender:
50% of the number of blocks in the licence area; or
if 50% of that number is a whole number and a fraction—the next higher whole number.
Subject to paragraph (4)(a), the blocks that remain in the licence area after a surrender under subsection (2) must form a discrete area.
Subject to subsection (5), the Designated Authority may:
give permission for the surrender of blocks in a licence area if the licence area remaining after the proposed surrender would consist of not more than 3 discrete areas; or
give permission for a licence area to be reduced by less than 50% if the Designated Authority considers that there are special circumstances present in relation to the renewal application.
The Designated Authority may give permission under subsection (4) only with the approval of the Joint Authority.
Subsection (5) does not apply to a block in an external territory offshore area.
Note: The responsible Commonwealth Minister is both the Designated Authority (see subsection 29(3)) and the Joint Authority (see subsection 32(3)) for an external territory offshore area.

section.heading: Request for further information

content.p: The Designated Authority may ask the applicant to provide further information about the application.
The request must:
be in writing; and
be given to the applicant; and
specify the time within which the information must be provided.
Information requested under subsection (1) must be provided:
in writing; and
within the time specified in the request.

section.heading: Payment of fee

content.p: The applicant must pay the application fee prescribed by the regulations.
The fee must be paid when the application is made.
The Joint Authority may refund any fee paid under subsection (1) but only if it is satisfied that special circumstances exist that justify the refund of the fee.

section.heading: Commonwealth-State offshore area—Designated Authority must refer renewal application to Joint Authority if certain requirements met

content.p: This section applies if the renewal application covers blocks in a Commonwealth-State offshore area.
If the applicant does what is required by sections 101 to 106, the Designated Authority must refer the application to the Joint Authority.
If the applicant does not do what is required by sections 101 to 106, the Designated Authority:
must not refer the application to the Joint Authority; and
must give the applicant written notice that the application has been refused.
The application lapses if a notice is given under subsection (3).

section.heading: Commonwealth-State offshore area—provisional renewal of an exploration licence

content.p: The Joint Authority for a Commonwealth-State offshore area must provisionally renew an exploration licence if:
the Designated Authority refers the renewal application to the Joint Authority under section 107; and
the applicant has complied with:
this Act; and
the regulations; and
the licence conditions.

Note 1: Under section 89, the renewal of the licence cannot be effective before it is registered (see section 334 for registration). The renewal will not be registered until it has been properly accepted (see section 114 for proper acceptance).
Note 2: Under section 118, new conditions may be imposed on renewal.
If subsection (1) does not require the Joint Authority to provisionally renew the licence, the Joint Authority may:
provisionally renew the licence; or
refuse to renew the licence.

section.heading: External territory offshore area—how application for renewal dealt with

content.p: This section applies if the renewal application covers blocks in an external territory offshore area.
If the applicant does not do what is required by sections 101 to 106, the responsible Commonwealth Minister (as the Joint Authority for the offshore area) must refuse to renew the licence.
If:
the applicant does what is required by sections 101 to 106; and
the applicant has complied with:
this Act; and
the regulations; and
the licence conditions;
the responsible Commonwealth Minister (as the Joint Authority for that offshore area) must provisionally renew the exploration licence.

Note 1: Under section 89, the renewal of the licence cannot be effective before it is registered (see section 334 for registration). The renewal will not be registered until it has been properly accepted (see section 114 for proper acceptance).
Note 2: Under section 118, new conditions may be imposed on renewal.
If:
subsection (2) does not require the responsible Commonwealth Minister to refuse to renew the licence; and
subsection (3) does not require the responsible Commonwealth Minister to provisionally renew the licence;
the responsible Commonwealth Minister (as the Joint Authority for that offshore area) may:
provisionally renew the licence; or
refuse to renew the licence.

Note: Under section 89, the renewal of the licence cannot be effective before it is registered (see section 334 for registration). The renewal will not be registered until it has been properly accepted (see section 114 for proper acceptance).

section.heading: Applicant must be notified

content.p: The Designated Authority must give the applicant written notice of the Joint Authority’s decision under section 108 or 109.
If the Joint Authority provisionally renews the exploration licence under section 108 or 109, the notice must contain the following information:
notification of the conditions of the renewed licence;
notification of any determination under section 399 that the applicant must lodge a security or a further security;
notification that the provisional renewal will lapse unless the applicant, before the end of the primary payment period:
gives the Designated Authority a written acceptance of the renewal; and
lodges any security required by the Joint Authority under section 399; and
pays the fees that must be paid under the Exploration Licence Fees Act.
Note: Section 118 provides for renewals to be granted subject to conditions.

section.heading: Amendment of conditions

content.p: If the licence holder:
has been provisionally granted a renewal of the licence under section 108 or 109; and
is notified of the licence conditions; and
is dissatisfied with a condition;
the holder may ask the Joint Authority to amend the condition.
The request must:
be made within 30 days after the day on which the holder is given notice under section 110; and
be lodged with the Designated Authority.
If the Joint Authority is given a request under subsection (1), the Joint Authority may amend the licence conditions.
The Joint Authority must give the holder written notice of the amendment.

section.heading: Amendment of security requirements

content.p: If the licence holder:
has been provisionally granted a renewal of the licence under section 108 or 109; and
is notified of a security requirement; and
is dissatisfied with the amount of the security required;
the holder may ask the Joint Authority to make a new determination under section 399.
The request must:
be made within 30 days after the day on which the holder is given notice under section 110; and
be lodged with the Designated Authority.
If the Joint Authority is given a request under subsection (1), the Authority may make a new determination under section 399.
The Joint Authority must give the holder written notice of the new determination.

section.heading: Extension of primary payment period

content.p: If the licence holder makes a request under section 111 or 112, the holder may ask the Designated Authority to extend the primary payment period.
The request must be made within 30 days after the day on which the holder is given notice under section 110.
If the Designated Authority agrees to the request, the Designated Authority must:
determine the period of the extension in writing; and
give the holder a written notice informing the holder of the period of the extension.

section.heading: Acceptance of renewal of exploration licence

content.p: The provisional renewal of an exploration licence is properly accepted by the licence holder if, before the end of the primary payment period, the holder:
gives the Designated Authority a written acceptance of the renewal; and
lodges any security required by the Joint Authority under section 399; and
pays the fees that must be paid under the Exploration Licence Fees Act.
Note: Under section 89, the renewal of the licence cannot be effective before it is registered (see section 334 for registration).
The provisional renewal of an exploration licence is properly accepted by the licence holder if the holder:
has been granted an extension of the primary payment period under section 113; and
before the end of the secondary payment period:
gives the Designated Authority a written acceptance of the renewal; and
lodges any security required by the Joint Authority under section 399; and
pays the fees that must be paid under the Exploration Licence Fees Act.
Note: Under section 89, the renewal of the licence cannot be effective before it is registered (see section 334 for registration).

section.heading: Conditions applicable to licence on renewal

content.p: If the provisional renewal is properly accepted, the renewed licence is subject to:
the conditions specified in the notice given to the licence holder under section 110; or
if the Joint Authority amended those conditions under section 111—those conditions as amended.

section.heading: Lapse of provisional renewal of exploration licence

content.p: If the provisional renewal of an exploration licence is not properly accepted under section 114, the provisional renewal lapses.

section.heading: General

content.p: The sources of obligations associated with an exploration licence are:
the licence conditions; and
obligations arising from compliance directions given by the Designated Authority; and
obligations imposed by this Act and the regulations.
Note: For paragraph (a) see sections 118 to 120. For paragraph (b) see sections 387 and 392. For paragraph (c) see sections 123 to 125 and section 372.
If an exploration licence has 2 or more holders, all the holders are jointly and severally bound by the obligations that attach to the licence.

section.heading: Conditions of exploration licence

content.p: The Joint Authority may grant or renew an exploration licence subject to whatever conditions the Joint Authority thinks appropriate.
If the Joint Authority grants or renews an exploration licence subject to conditions, the conditions must be specified in the licence.
Without limiting subsection (1), the Joint Authority may attach the following kinds of conditions to the grant or renewal of an exploration licence:
a condition requiring the licence holder to take out insurance as required by the Designated Authority;

a condition requiring the holder to carry out certain work in or in relation to the licence area during the term of the licence, and to comply with directions concerning that work given under section 387;

a condition requiring the holder to spend a specified amount of money in carrying out the work referred to in paragraph (b), and to comply with directions concerning that expenditure given under section 387;
a condition requiring the holder to lodge a security with the Designated Authority;
a condition requiring the holder to keep specified information;
a condition requiring the holder to give the Designated Authority, on request, specified information;
a condition requiring the holder to take steps to protect the environment of the licence area, including conditions relating to:
protecting wildlife; or
minimising the effect on the environment of the licence area and the area surrounding the licence area of activities carried out in the licence area;
a condition requiring the holder to repair any damage to the environment caused by activities in the licence area;
a condition requiring the holder to pay a specified penalty to the Commonwealth if the holder does not comply with a licence condition.
A condition under paragraph (3)(d) must specify:
the amount of the security required; and
the kind of security required; and
the manner and form in which the security is to be lodged.
Without limiting paragraph (3)(d), a condition under that paragraph may require the lodgment of a security in the form of a guarantee and if a guarantee is required the condition may specify:
the kind of person who is to give the guarantee; and
the terms of the guarantee.

section.heading: No conditions requiring payment of money

content.p: Except for a condition requiring the payment of a penalty or lodgment of security, a licence condition must not require the payment of money to:
the Designated Authority; or
the Joint Authority; or
the Commonwealth.

section.heading: Variation of conditions

content.p: If:
an exploration licence holder requests the Designated Authority in writing to vary a licence condition; or
an exploration licence continues in force because of section 93; or
an extension of an exploration licence is granted under section 95; or
part of the licence area of an exploration licence is surrendered under section 99 or 100;
the Joint Authority may vary a licence condition.
If a Designated Authority gives:
a direction under section 387; or
an approval, consent or exemption under the regulations;

to an exploration licence holder, the Joint Authority may vary a licence condition to the extent necessary to avoid inconsistency between the licence conditions and the direction, approval, consent or exemption.
The Joint Authority may vary a licence condition subject to whatever conditions the Joint Authority thinks appropriate.
If the Joint Authority varies a licence condition, the Designated Authority must give the licence holder a written notice that:
informs the holder of the variation; and
specifies the conditions which have been varied; and
specifies any conditions to which the variation is subject.

section.heading: Exemption from or suspension of conditions

content.p: If:
an exploration licence holder requests the Designated Authority in writing to:
suspend a licence condition; or
exempt the holder from complying with a licence condition; or
an exploration licence continues in force because of section 93; or
an extension of an exploration licence is granted under section 95; or
part of the licence area of an exploration licence is surrendered under section 99 or 100;
the Joint Authority may:
suspend a licence condition; or
exempt the holder from complying with a licence condition.
If a Designated Authority gives:
a direction under section 387; or
an approval, consent or exemption under the regulations;

to an exploration licence holder, the Joint Authority may suspend a licence condition, or exempt the holder from compliance with a licence condition, to the extent necessary to avoid inconsistency between the licence conditions and the direction, approval, consent or exemption.
The Joint Authority may:
suspend a licence condition; or
exempt the licence holder from complying with a licence condition;
subject to whatever conditions the Joint Authority thinks appropriate.
If the Joint Authority:
suspends a licence condition; or
exempts the licence holder from complying with a licence condition;
the Designated Authority must give the holder a written notice that:
informs the holder of the exemption or suspension; and
specifies the conditions which have been suspended or affected by the exemption; and
specifies any conditions to which the suspension or exemption is subject.
Note: A suspension or exemption of a condition cannot be effective before it is registered (see section 337).

section.heading: Automatic suspension of conditions if licence rights are suspended

content.p: If:
the Joint Authority suspends particular rights conferred by an exploration licence under section 48; and
a licence condition is affected by the suspension;
the licence condition is suspended for the period of the suspension of the rights.

section.heading: Work practices

content.p: If a person who is:
an exploration licence holder; or
an associate of the holder;
carries out activities in the licence area that are authorised by the licence, the person must take all reasonable steps:
to ensure that the activities are carried out at a standard that is accepted as reasonable and proper in the mining industry; and
to protect the health, safety and welfare of people engaged in the activities in and about the licence area; and
to maintain in good repair all structures and equipment brought into the licence area by the person; and
to remove from the licence area any structure, equipment or other property that:
belongs to the person, or is under the person’s control; and
is not being used, or is not going to be used, in connection with the activities.
Penalty: 200 penalty units.

section.heading: Licence holder must keep specified records etc.

content.p: An exploration licence holder must:
keep whatever records, cores and samples; and
give whatever records, cores and samples to the Designated Authority for inspection; and
make whatever returns;
are necessary to comply with:
the regulations; or
the licence conditions; or
a direction given by the Designated Authority under section 387.
Note: Under section 387 the Designated Authority may direct a person to keep records and cores, to collect and retain samples, and to make returns.
Penalty: 100 penalty units.

section.heading: Licence holder must assist inspectors

content.p: An exploration licence holder must provide an inspector with reasonable facilities and assistance so that the inspector is able to carry out compliance inspections.
Note: See sections 377 to 384 for compliance inspections.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: General

content.p: An exploration licence expires if:
the term of the licence ends without the licence being renewed; or
the licence holder surrenders the licence; or
a retention licence is granted over the blocks in the licence area of the exploration licence; or
a mining licence is granted over the blocks in the licence area of the exploration licence; or
the licence is cancelled.
Note: For paragraph (a) see Division 6. For paragraph (b) see section 127. For paragraph (c) see section 128. For paragraph (d) see section 129. For paragraph (e) see section 130.

section.heading: Voluntary surrender of exploration licence

content.p: An exploration licence holder may surrender the licence.
Note 1: See Division 5 for voluntary surrender of part of a licence area.
Note 2: The surrender takes effect when it is registered under section 337 (see subsection 337(5)).

section.heading: Automatic expiry of exploration licence when retention licence takes effect

content.p: If:
an exploration licence is in force under this Act; and
the Joint Authority provisionally grants a retention licence over all or some of the blocks in the exploration licence area; and
the provisional grant of the retention licence is properly accepted; and
the retention licence comes into force;
the exploration licence expires in relation to the blocks covered by the retention licence.

section.heading: Automatic expiry of exploration licence when mining licence takes effect

content.p: If:
an exploration licence is in force under this Act; and
the Joint Authority provisionally grants a mining licence over all or some of the blocks in the exploration licence area; and
the provisional grant of the mining licence is properly accepted; and
the mining licence comes into force;
the exploration licence expires in relation to the blocks covered by the mining licence.

section.heading: Cancellation of exploration licence

content.p: Subject to subsection (5), the Joint Authority may cancel an exploration licence if the licence holder:
breaches a licence condition; or
contravenes a provision of this Act or the regulations; or
breaches a condition attached to an approval under subsection 365(2); or
fails to pay user charge that is payable for the licence under the Exploration Licence User Charge Act.
If the Joint Authority proposes to cancel a licence under subsection (1), the Designated Authority must give the licence holder a written notice that informs the holder of the proposed cancellation.
The notice must:
specify the reason for the proposed cancellation; and
invite the holder to make submissions in relation to the proposed cancellation; and
specify the day by which submissions should be given to the Joint Authority; and
specify an address where submissions are to be lodged.
The day specified under paragraph (3)(c) must be not less than 60 days after the day on which the notice is given.
The Joint Authority may cancel the licence only if:
the holder has been given a notice under subsection (2); and
the Joint Authority has considered:
any submission made by the holder; and
any steps taken by the holder to remedy the circumstances that led to the proposal to cancel the licence and to prevent those circumstances from happening again; and
the Joint Authority is satisfied that no special circumstances exist that justify the licence not being cancelled.

section.heading: Obligations of former exploration licence holders and former associates

content.p: Subject to subsection (4), if:
a person was:
an exploration licence holder; or
an associate of an exploration licence holder; and
the licence:
expires; or
is cancelled; or
is surrendered; and
an obligation associated with the licence arising out of:
a licence condition; or
a direction given under section 387; or
this Act or the regulations;
has not been discharged; and
the person was bound by that obligation when the person was the licence holder or an associate;
the person remains bound by the obligation until the obligation is discharged.
Subsection (1) does not continue an obligation to carry out exploration or recovery activities.
Subsection (1) continues an obligation that a person had to carry out exploration or recovery activities in a particular manner if the person carries them out.
The Joint Authority may determine that the person is not subject to:
a particular obligation under this section; or
all the person’s remaining obligations under this section.
A determination under subsection (4) is to be in writing.

section.heading: Retention licences

content.p: This Part provides for the grant of retention licences over blocks in an offshore area.
Note: A retention licence is designed to allow an exploration licence holder to retain rights over an area if:

item.p: the holder has identified and evaluated a significant mineral deposit in the exploration licence area; and

mining the deposit is not commercially viable in the short term for some reason (for example, the political situation, the prevailing situation in the commodity market for particular minerals, the need to arrange finance or build up capital reserves, the need to develop new technologies or the impending development of new technologies); and
there is a reasonable prospect of development of the deposit in the longer term.

content.p: See section 145 for the grounds on which a retention licence may be granted.

section.heading: Activities authorised by a retention licence

content.p: Subject to subsections (2) and (3), a retention licence holder may:
explore for minerals in the licence area; and
recover minerals in the licence area.
Note 1: The retention licence may specify a restricted range of activities that are the only ones authorised by the licence (see subsection 146(3)).
Note 2: Under subsection 23(1) the concept of exploration extends to activities that are directly related to exploration.
Note 3: Under subsection 24(1) the concept of recovery extends to activities that are directly related to the recovery of minerals.
A retention licence does not authorise the recovery of minerals as part of a commercial mining operation.
If the licence is expressed to restrict the kind of minerals covered by the licence, the holder is not permitted to explore for, or to recover, minerals not covered by the licence.
A restriction on the kind of minerals covered by the licence may be inclusive (for example, only minerals A, B and C) or exclusive (for example, all minerals except A, B and C).
For the purposes of subsection (3), the holder does not recover an excluded mineral if, in the course of exploring for, or recovering, another mineral, the holder recovers some excluded mineral.

section.heading: Joint Authority may cancel or not renew retention licence without compensation

content.p: No compensation is payable because of the cancellation or non-renewal of a retention licence by the Joint Authority.
Note 1: The Joint Authority may cancel the licence under section 189 or 190.
Note 2: The Joint Authority may refuse under section 165 or 166 to renew the licence.

section.heading: Licence rights may be suspended

content.p: The Joint Authority must suspend particular rights conferred by a retention licence if the Joint Authority is satisfied that it is necessary in the national interest to do so.
The Joint Authority may suspend rights under subsection (1) for a specified period or for an indefinite period.
The Joint Authority may end a suspension at any time.
A suspension or the ending of a suspension must be in writing.
If the Joint Authority:
suspends rights conferred by a retention licence; or
ends a suspension;
the Joint Authority must give the licence holder a written notice that informs the holder of the suspension or the ending of a suspension.
Note: See section 181 for the effect of the suspension on the obligations associated with the licence.
A suspension takes effect when:
the holder has been given notice of the suspension under subsection (5); and
the suspension has been registered under section 337.

section.heading: Compensation for acquisition of property due to suspension of rights

content.p: If:
the Joint Authority suspends licence rights under section 135; and
the suspension results in the acquisition of property from a person; and
the Commonwealth and the person agree on an amount of compensation for the acquisition;
the Commonwealth must pay the person the agreed amount of compensation.
If:
the Joint Authority suspends licence rights under section 135; and
the suspension results in the acquisition of property from a person; and
the Commonwealth and the person do not agree on an amount of compensation for the acquisition; and
the person brings an action for compensation against the Commonwealth in the High Court or an appropriate Supreme Court;
the Commonwealth must pay the person the amount of compensation (if any) that is determined by the court.
In this section:
acquisition of property means an acquisition of property within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxxi) of the Constitution.
appropriate Supreme Court means the Supreme Court of, or having jurisdiction in, the State or Territory for which the Joint Authority is established.

division.heading: Application for and grant of retention licence

section.heading: Application for retention licence

content.p: An exploration licence holder may apply to the Joint Authority for a retention licence over blocks within the exploration licence area.
A person may apply for a retention licence over a group of blocks only if:
the group forms a discrete area; and
there are not more than 20 blocks in the group.
The exploration licence holder may apply for 2 or more retention licences over different parts of the exploration licence area.

section.heading: How to apply

content.p: The application must:
be made in accordance with the approved form; and
be made in the approved manner; and
specify the blocks for which the application is made; and
include details of:
the reasons why the applicant is applying for a retention licence rather than a mining licence; and
the mineral deposit that the applicant has identified and evaluated and that the applicant believes is commercially viable in the longer term; and
the applicant’s assessment of the present and potential commercial viability of the mineral deposit; and
the overall work program that the applicant has already carried out under the exploration licence on the blocks covered by the application; and
the amount of money that the applicant has already spent under the exploration licence on and in connection with the blocks covered by the application; and
the activities that the applicant intends to carry out on the blocks covered by the application; and
the amount of money that the applicant intends to spend on and in connection with those activities; and
the technical qualifications of the applicant and of the applicant’s employees who are likely to be involved in activities authorised by the licence; and
the technical advice available to the applicant; and
the financial resources available to the applicant; and
be accompanied by maps that:
relate to the blocks; and
comply with guidelines issued by the Designated Authority under subsection 41(2); and
specify an address for service of notices under this Act and the regulations.
Note: For paragraphs (a) and (b) see section 41.
The mineral deposit details given under subparagraph (1)(d)(ii) must include:
a full description of the mineral deposit; and
both factual information about the deposit and the applicant’s interpretation of the factual information.
The applicant may include in the application any other information that the applicant thinks is relevant.
The application must be lodged with the Designated Authority.

section.heading: Payment of fee

content.p: The applicant must pay the application fee prescribed by the regulations.
The fee must be paid when the application is made.
The Joint Authority may refund any fee paid under subsection (1) but only if it is satisfied that special circumstances exist that justify the refund of the fee.

section.heading: Application must be advertised

content.p: The applicant must advertise the application in a newspaper circulating throughout the State or external territory concerned.
The advertisement must contain:
the applicant’s name and address; and
a map and description of the blocks applied for that are sufficient for the blocks to be identified; and
the address of the Designated Authority; and
a statement:
that the applicant has applied for a retention licence for the blocks described in the notice; and
that invites comment from the public on the application; and
that requests that comments be sent to the applicant and the Designated Authority within 30 days after the day on which the advertisement is published.
The advertisement must be published as soon as possible after the applicant applies for a retention licence.
Subject to subsection (5), the advertisement must be published within 14 days after the day on which the applicant lodges the application.
If:
the applicant applies to the Designated Authority within the 14 day period referred to in subsection (4) for an extension of the period; and
the Designated Authority extends the period;
the advertisement must be published within the period as extended by the Designated Authority.

section.heading: Request for further information

content.p: The Designated Authority may ask the applicant for further information about the application.
The request must:
be in writing; and
be given to the applicant; and
specify the time within which the information must be provided.
Information requested under subsection (1) must be provided:
in writing; and
within the time specified in the request.

section.heading: Commonwealth-State offshore area—Designated Authority must refer application to Joint Authority if certain requirements met

content.p: This section applies if the application covers blocks in a Commonwealth-State offshore area.
If the applicant does what is required by sections 138 to 141, the Designated Authority must refer the application to the Joint Authority.
If the applicant does not do what is required by sections 138 to 141, the Designated Authority:
must not refer the application to the Joint Authority; and
must give the applicant written notice that the application has been refused.
The application lapses if a notice is given under subsection (3).

section.heading: Commonwealth-State offshore area—Joint Authority may provisionally grant retention licence

content.p: If the Designated Authority for a Commonwealth-State offshore area refers the application to the Joint Authority under section 142, the Joint Authority may:
subject to section 145, provisionally grant a retention licence to the applicant; or
refuse the application.

Note: Under section 154, the grant of the licence cannot be effective before it is registered (see section 333 for registration). The grant will not be registered until it has been properly accepted (see section 151 for proper acceptance).

section.heading: External territory offshore area—how application for retention licence dealt with

content.p: This section applies if the application covers blocks in an external territory offshore area.
If the applicant does not do what is required by sections 137 to 141, the responsible Commonwealth Minister (as the Joint Authority for the offshore area) must refuse the application.
If the applicant does what is required by sections 137 to 141, the responsible Commonwealth Minister (as the Joint Authority for the offshore area) may:
subject to section 145, provisionally grant a retention licence to the applicant; or
refuse the application.

Note: Under section 154, the grant of the licence cannot be effective before it is registered (see section 333 for registration). The grant will not be registered until it has been properly accepted (see section 151 for proper acceptance).

section.heading: Grounds for granting retention licence

content.p: The Joint Authority may provisionally grant the retention licence only if it is satisfied that:
the exploration licence holder has identified and evaluated a significant mineral deposit in the exploration licence area; and
there are reasonable grounds for the holder not applying immediately for a mining licence.
Without limiting subsection (1), reasonable grounds for not applying immediately for a mining licence include the following:
the need to obtain government approvals (for example, relating to environmental protection) before mining activities can commence;
the need to carry out further exploration or evaluation in order to establish the commercial viability of a mineral deposit found in the licence area;
the need to develop technologies before mining activities can commence;
the need to arrange finance, or to secure additional capital reserves, before mining activities can commence;

the existence of economic considerations (for example, the prevailing condition of the commodity market for the minerals concerned) that effectively preclude mining activities in the immediate future;
the existence of political considerations that effectively preclude mining activities in the immediate future.

section.heading: Matters to be specified in the licence

content.p: The licence must specify:
the blocks covered by the licence; and
the term of the licence; and
the licence conditions.
The term specified under paragraph (1)(b) is not to exceed 5 years.
The licence may specify the activities that may be carried out under the licence.
If the licence includes a specification under subsection (3), the licence authorises only the specified activities.

section.heading: Applicant must be notified

content.p: The Designated Authority must give the applicant written notice of the Joint Authority’s decision under section 143 or 144.
If the Joint Authority provisionally grants a retention licence:
the Designated Authority must give the licence to the provisional holder; and
the notice under subsection (1) must contain the following information:
notification of any determination under section 399 that the provisional holder must lodge a security;
notification that the provisional grant will lapse unless the provisional holder, before the end of the primary payment period:
(A) gives the Designated Authority a written acceptance of the grant; and
(B) lodges any security required by the Joint Authority under section 399; and
(C) pays the fees that must be paid for the licence under the Retention Licence Fees Act.

section.heading: Amendment of conditions

content.p: If the provisional holder is dissatisfied with a licence condition, the provisional holder may ask the Joint Authority to amend the condition.
The request must:
be made within 30 days after the day on which the provisional holder is given the licence under section 147; and
be lodged with the Designated Authority.
If the Joint Authority receives a request under subsection (1), the Joint Authority may amend the licence conditions.
The Joint Authority must give the provisional holder written notice of the amendment.

section.heading: Amendment of security requirements

content.p: If the provisional holder:
is notified of a security requirement; and
is dissatisfied with the amount of the security required;
the provisional holder may ask the Joint Authority to make a new determination under section 399.
The request must:
be made within 30 days after the day on which the provisional holder is given notice under section 147; and
be lodged with the Designated Authority.
If the Joint Authority receives a request under subsection (1), the Joint Authority may make a new determination under section 399.
The Joint Authority must give the provisional holder written notice of the new determination.

section.heading: Extension of primary payment period

content.p: If the provisional holder makes a request under section 148 or 149, the provisional holder may ask the Designated Authority to extend the primary payment period.
The request must be made within 30 days after the day on which the provisional holder is given notice under section 147.
If the Designated Authority agrees to the request, the Designated Authority must:
determine the period of the extension; and
give the provisional holder a written notice informing the applicant of the period of the extension.

section.heading: Acceptance of grant of retention licence

content.p: The provisional grant of a retention licence is properly accepted by the provisional holder if, before the end of the primary payment period, the provisional holder:
gives the Designated Authority a written acceptance of the grant; and
lodges any security for the licence required by the Joint Authority under section 399; and
pays the fees that must be paid for the licence under the Retention Licence Fees Act.
A retention licence provisionally granted under section 143 or 144 is properly accepted by the provisional holder if the provisional holder:
has been granted an extension of the primary payment period under section 150; and
before the end of the secondary payment period:
gives the Designated Authority a written acceptance of the grant; and
lodges any security required by the Joint Authority under section 399; and
pays the fees that must be paid for the licence under the Retention Licence Fees Act.
Note: Under section 154, the grant of the licence cannot be effective before the grant is registered (see section 333 for registration).

section.heading: Conditions applicable to licence on grant

content.p: If the provisional grant of the licence is properly accepted, it is subject to:
the conditions specified in the licence given to the applicant under section 147; or
if the Joint Authority amended those conditions under section 148—those conditions as amended.

section.heading: Lapse of provisional grant of retention licence

content.p: If the provisional grant of the licence is not properly accepted under section 151, the provisional grant lapses.

section.heading: Initial term of retention licence

content.p: A retention licence comes into force on:
the day on which the grant of the licence is registered; or
if a day later than the day on which the grant of the licence is registered is specified in the licence as its commencement day—that specified day.
The initial term of a retention licence expires at the end of the period specified in the licence under subsection 146(1).
Note 1: For the maximum initial term see subsection 146(2).
Note 2: The licence may be surrendered at any time (see section 187).
The period runs from:
the day on which the licence is provisionally granted; or
if a day later than the day on which the licence is provisionally granted is specified in the licence as its commencement day—that specified day.

section.heading: Term of renewal of licence

content.p: A renewal of a retention licence comes into force on:
the day on which the renewal is registered; or
the day on which the previous term of the licence expires;
whichever is the later.
Note: See Division 5 for renewal.
The term of a renewal of a licence expires at the end of the period specified in the notice under section 169.
Note 1: For the maximum term of renewal see subsection 169(3).
Note 2: The licence may be surrendered at any time (see section 187).
The period runs from the expiry of the previous term of the licence.
Ignore section 156 in working out the period referred to in subsection (3).

section.heading: Effect of application for renewal on term of retention licence

content.p: If:
a retention licence holder applies to renew the licence under section 159; and
the current term of the licence expires; and
a renewal of the licence does not take effect immediately after the current term expires;
the licence remains in force after the current term expires until:
a renewal of the licence takes effect; or
a provisional renewal of the licence lapses; or
the application for renewal is withdrawn or refused.

section.heading: Effect of application for mining licence on term of retention licence

content.p: If:
a retention licence holder applies for a mining licence over the licence area, or part of the licence area, of the retention licence; and
the current term of the retention licence expires; and
a grant of the mining licence does not take effect before the current term of the retention licence expires;
the retention licence remains in force until:
the grant of the mining licence takes effect; or
a provisional grant of the mining licence lapses; or
the application for the mining licence is withdrawn or refused.

division.heading: Voluntary surrender of part of retention licence area

section.heading: Voluntary surrender of blocks if discrete area remains

content.p: A retention licence holder may surrender a block or some of the blocks covered by the licence if the remaining blocks in the licence area form a discrete area.
Note: See section 187 for the surrender of the whole licence.
A surrender under subsection (1):
must be made in a written notice; and
must identify the blocks surrendered; and
must be given to the Designated Authority.
Note: The surrender takes effect when it is registered under section 337 (see subsection 337(5)).

division.heading: Application for and grant of renewal of retention licence

section.heading: Application for renewal of retention licence

content.p: A retention licence holder may apply to the Joint Authority to renew the licence.
Note: At each renewal, the licence conditions are reviewed (see section 177).

section.heading: When must an application to renew be made?

content.p: Subject to subsection (2), the application must be made at least 6 months before the day on which the licence is to expire.
The Designated Authority may accept an application that is made later than 6 months before the day on which the licence is to expire if:
the application is made before the day on which the licence expires; and
the Designated Authority believes that there are reasonable grounds for accepting the application.

section.heading: How to apply for renewal

content.p: The application must:
be made in accordance with the approved form; and
be made in the approved manner; and
include details of:
the reasons why the applicant is applying to renew the retention licence rather than applying for a mining licence; and
the activities carried out by the applicant under the licence during its current term; and
the amount of money spent by the applicant in relation to the blocks covered by the licence during its current term; and
the results obtained by the applicant from carrying out the activities referred to in subparagraph (ii); and
the activities that the applicant intends to carry out under the licence during the term applied for; and
the amount of money that the applicant intends to spend in relation to activities authorised by the licence during the term applied for.
Note: For paragraphs (a) and (b) see section 41.
The applicant may include in the application any other information that the applicant thinks is relevant.
The application must be lodged with the Designated Authority.

section.heading: Request for further information

content.p: The Designated Authority may ask the applicant to provide further information relating to the application.
The request must:
be in writing; and
be given to the applicant; and
specify the time within which the information must be provided.
Information requested under subsection (1) must be provided:
in writing; and
within the time specified in the request.

section.heading: Payment of fee

content.p: The applicant must pay the application fee prescribed by the regulations.
The fee must be paid when the application is made.
The Joint Authority may refund any fee paid under subsection (1) but only if it is satisfied that special circumstances exist that justify the refund of the fee.

section.heading: Commonwealth-State offshore area—Designated Authority must refer renewal application to Joint Authority if certain requirements met

content.p: This section applies if the renewal application covers blocks in a Commonwealth-State offshore area.
If the applicant does what is required by sections 161 to 163, the Designated Authority must refer the application to the Joint Authority.
If the applicant does not do what is required by sections 161 to 163, the Designated Authority:
must not refer the application to the Joint Authority; and
must give the applicant written notice that the application has been refused.
The application lapses if a notice is given under subsection (3).

section.heading: Commonwealth-State offshore area—provisional renewal of retention licence

content.p: If the Designated Authority for a Commonwealth-State offshore area refers the application to the Joint Authority under section 164, the Joint Authority may:
provisionally renew the licence; or
subject to section 168, refuse to renew the licence.

Note 1: Under section 155, the renewal of the licence cannot be effective before it is registered (see section 334 for registration). The renewal will not be registered until it has been properly accepted (see section 173 for proper acceptance).
Note 2: Under section 177, new conditions may be imposed on renewal.

section.heading: External territory offshore area—how application for renewal dealt with

content.p: This section applies if the renewal application covers blocks in an external territory offshore area.
If the applicant does not do what is required by sections 161 to 163, the responsible Commonwealth Minister (as the Joint Authority for the offshore area) must refuse to renew the licence.
If the applicant does what is required by sections 161 to 163, the responsible Commonwealth Minister (as the Joint Authority for that offshore area) may:
provisionally renew the licence; or
subject to section 168, refuse to renew the licence.

Note 1: Under section 155, the renewal of the licence cannot be effective before it is registered (see section 334 for registration). The renewal will not be registered until it has been properly accepted (see section 173 for proper acceptance).
Note 2: Under section 177, new conditions may be imposed on renewal.

section.heading: Matters to be taken into account in deciding whether to renew retention licence

content.p: In determining whether to renew the licence, the Joint Authority may have regard to:
whether mining activities are commercially viable in the retention licence area; and
whether the applicant has complied with:
this Act; and
the regulations; and
any licence conditions.

section.heading: Refusal of application for renewal

content.p: If the Joint Authority proposes to refuse to renew the licence, the Designated Authority must give the applicant notice of the proposed refusal.

Note: The retention licence remains in force until the application for renewal has been finally determined (i.e. until the Joint Authority decides whether or not to renew the licence) (see section 156).
The notice must:
be in writing; and
give details of the Joint Authority’s reasons for its proposal not to renew the licence; and
invite the applicant to make written submissions on the proposed non-renewal to the Designated Authority; and
specify the day by which submissions should be made to the Designated Authority.
The day specified under paragraph (2)(d) is to be at least 30 days after the day on which the notice under subsection (1) is given to the applicant.
The Joint Authority, in deciding whether to refuse to renew the licence, must have regard to any submissions made by the applicant in response to the notice under subsection (1).

section.heading: Applicant must be notified

content.p: The Designated Authority must give the applicant written notice of the Joint Authority’s decision under section 165 or 166.
If the Joint Authority provisionally renews the licence under section 165 or 166, the notice must contain the following information:
notification of the term of the renewal;
notification of the conditions of the renewed licence;
notification of any determination under section 399 that the applicant must lodge a security or a further security;
notification that the provisional renewal will lapse unless the applicant, before the end of the primary payment period:
gives the Designated Authority a written acceptance of the renewal; and
lodges any security required by the Joint Authority under section 399; and
pays the fees that must be paid under the Retention Licence Fees Act.
Note: Paragraph (b): section 177 provides for renewals to be granted to conditions.
The term specified under paragraph (2)(a) is not to be more than 5 years.

section.heading: Amendment of conditions

content.p: If the licence holder:
has been provisionally granted a renewal of the licence under section 165 or 166; and
is notified of the licence conditions; and
is dissatisfied with a condition;
the holder may ask the Joint Authority to amend the condition.
The request must:
be made within 30 days after the day on which the applicant is given notice under section 169; and
be lodged with the Designated Authority.
If the Joint Authority is given a request under subsection (1), the Joint Authority may amend the licence conditions.
The Designated Authority must give the holder written notice of the amendment.

section.heading: Amendment of security requirements

content.p: If the licence holder:
has been provisionally granted a renewal of the licence under section 165 or 166; and
is notified of a security requirement; and
is dissatisfied with the amount of the security required;
the holder may ask the Joint Authority to make a new determination under section 399.
The request must:
be made within 30 days after the day on which the holder is given notice under section 169; and
be lodged with the Designated Authority.
If the Joint Authority is given a request under subsection (1), the Joint Authority may make a new determination under section 399.
The Designated Authority must give the holder written notice of the new determination.

section.heading: Extension of primary payment period

content.p: If the licence holder makes a request under section 170 or 171, the holder may ask the Designated Authority to extend the primary payment period.
The request must be made within 30 days after the day on which the holder is given notice under section 169.
If the Designated Authority agrees to the request to extend the primary payment period, the Designated Authority must:
determine the period of the extension in writing; and
give the holder a written notice informing the holder of the period of the extension.

section.heading: Acceptance of renewal of retention licence

content.p: The provisional renewal of a retention licence is properly accepted by the licence holder if, before the end of the primary payment period, the holder:
gives the Designated Authority a written acceptance of the renewal; and
lodges any security required by the Joint Authority under section 399; and
pays the fees that must be under the Retention Licence Fees Act.
Note: Under section 155, the renewal of the licence cannot be effective before it is registered (see section 334 for registration).
The provisional renewal of a retention licence is properly accepted by the licence holder if the holder:
has been granted an extension of the primary payment period under section 172; and
before the end of the secondary payment period:
gives the Designated Authority a written acceptance of the renewal; and
lodges any security required by the Joint Authority under section 399; and
pays the fees that must be paid under the Retention Licence Fees Act.
Note: Under section 155, the renewal of the licence cannot be effective before it is registered (see section 334 for registration).

section.heading: Conditions applicable to licence on renewal

content.p: If the provisional renewal is properly accepted, the renewed licence is subject to:
the conditions specified in the notice given to the licence holder under section 169; or
if the Joint Authority amended those conditions under section 170—those conditions as amended.

section.heading: Lapse of provisional renewal of retention licence

content.p: If the provisional renewal of a retention licence is not properly accepted under section 173, the provisional renewal lapses.

section.heading: General

content.p: The sources of obligations associated with a retention licence are:
the licence conditions; and
obligations arising from compliance directions given by the Designated Authority; and
obligations imposed by this Act and the regulations.
Note: For paragraph (a) see section 177. For paragraph (b) see section 387. For paragraph (c) see sections 177 to 185 and section 372.
If a retention licence has 2 or more holders, all the holders are jointly and severally bound by the obligations that attach to the licence.

section.heading: Conditions of retention licence

content.p: The Joint Authority may grant or renew a retention licence subject to whatever conditions the Joint Authority thinks appropriate.
If the Joint Authority grants or renews a retention licence subject to conditions, the conditions must be specified in the licence.
Without limiting subsection (1), the Joint Authority may attach the following kinds of conditions to the grant or renewal of a retention licence:
a condition requiring the licence holder to take out insurance as required by the Designated Authority;

a condition requiring the holder to carry out certain activities in or in relation to the licence area during the term of the licence, and to comply with directions concerning those activities given under section 387;

a condition requiring the holder to spend a specified amount of money in carrying out the activities referred to in paragraph (b), and to comply with directions concerning that expenditure given under section 387;
a condition requiring the holder to lodge a security with the Designated Authority;
a condition requiring the holder to keep specified information;
a condition requiring the holder to give the Designated Authority, on request, specified information;
a condition requiring the holder to take steps to protect the environment of the licence area, including conditions relating to:
protecting wildlife; or
minimising the effect on the environment of the licence area and the area surrounding the licence area of activities carried out in the licence area;
a condition requiring the holder to repair any damage to the environment caused by activities in the licence area;
a condition requiring the holder to pay a specified penalty to the Commonwealth if the holder does not comply with a licence condition.
A condition under paragraph (3)(d) must specify:
the amount of the security required; and
the kind of security required; and
the manner and form in which the security is to be lodged.
Without limiting paragraph (3)(d), a condition under that paragraph may require the lodgment of a security in the form of a guarantee and if a guarantee is required the condition may specify:
the kind of person who is to give the guarantee; and
the terms of the guarantee.

section.heading: No conditions requiring payment of money

content.p: Except for a condition requiring the payment of a penalty or lodgment of a security, a licence condition must not require the payment of money to:
the Designated Authority; or
the Joint Authority; or
the Commonwealth.

section.heading: Variation of conditions

content.p: If:
a retention licence holder requests the Designated Authority in writing to vary a licence condition; or
part of the licence area of a retention licence is surrendered under section 158;
the Joint Authority may vary a licence condition.
If a Designated Authority gives:
a direction under section 387; or
an approval, consent or exemption under the regulations;

to a retention licence holder, the Joint Authority may vary a licence condition to the extent necessary to avoid inconsistency between the licence conditions and the direction, approval, consent or exemption.
The Joint Authority may vary a licence condition subject to whatever conditions the Joint Authority thinks appropriate.
If the Joint Authority varies a licence condition, the Designated Authority must give the licence holder a written notice that:
informs the holder of the variation; and
specifies the conditions which have been varied; and
specifies any conditions to which the variation is subject.

section.heading: Exemption from or suspension of conditions

content.p: If:
a retention licence holder requests the Designated Authority in writing to:
suspend a licence condition; or
exempt the holder from complying with a licence condition; or
part of the licence area of a retention licence is surrendered under section 158;
the Joint Authority may:
suspend a licence condition; or
exempt the holder from complying with a licence condition.
If a Designated Authority gives:
a direction under section 387; or
an approval, consent or exemption under the regulations;

to a retention licence holder, the Joint Authority may suspend a licence condition, or exempt the holder from compliance with a licence condition, to the extent necessary to avoid inconsistency between the licence conditions and the direction, approval, consent or exemption.
The Joint Authority may:
suspend a licence condition; or
exempt the licence holder from compliance with a licence condition;
subject to whatever conditions the Joint Authority thinks appropriate.
If the Joint Authority:
suspends a licence condition; or
exempts the licence holder from complying with a licence condition;
the Designated Authority must give the holder a written notice that:
informs the holder of the exemption or suspension; and
specifies the conditions which have been suspended or affected by the exemption; and
specifies any conditions to which the suspension or exemption is subject.
Note: A suspension or exemption of a condition does not take effect until registered (see section 337).

section.heading: Automatic suspension of conditions if licence rights are suspended

content.p: If:
the Joint Authority suspends particular rights conferred by a retention licence under section 135; and
a licence condition is affected by the suspension;
the licence condition is suspended for the period of the suspension of the rights.

section.heading: Significant changes in circumstances to be reported to Designated Authority

content.p: A retention licence holder must notify the Designated Authority of any change of circumstances that significantly affects the long term viability of mining activities in the retention licence area.
Note: The Joint Authority may cancel the retention licence if it believes that circumstances have changed so that mining activities can now commence (see section 190).
Subsection (1) applies to a change of circumstances whether favourable or unfavourable to the long term viability of mining activities in the retention licence area.

section.heading: Work practices

content.p: If a person who is:
a retention licence holder; or
an associate of the holder;
carries out activities in the licence area that are authorised by the licence, the person must take all reasonable steps:
to ensure that the activities are carried out at a standard that is accepted as reasonable and proper in the mining industry; and
to protect the health, safety and welfare of people engaged in the activities in and about the licence area; and
to maintain in good repair all structures and equipment in the licence area brought there by the person; and
to remove from the licence area any structure, equipment or other property that:
belongs to the person, or is under the person’s control; and
is not being used, or is not going to be used, in connection with the activities.
Penalty: 200 penalty units.

section.heading: Licence holder must keep specified records etc.

content.p: A retention licence holder must:
keep whatever records, cores and samples; and
give whatever records, cores and samples to the Designated Authority for inspection; and
make whatever returns;
are necessary to comply with:
the regulations; or
the licence conditions; or
a direction given by the Designated Authority under section 387.
Note: Under section 387 the Designated Authority may direct a person to keep records and cores, to collect and retain samples, and to make returns.
Penalty: 100 penalty units.

section.heading: Licence holder must assist inspectors

content.p: A retention licence holder must provide an inspector with reasonable facilities and assistance so that the inspector is able to carry out compliance inspections.
Note: See sections 377 to 384 for compliance inspections.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: General

content.p: A retention licence expires if:
the term of the licence expires without the licence being renewed; or
the licence holder surrenders the licence; or
a mining licence is granted over the blocks in the licence area of the retention licence; or
the licence is cancelled.
Note: For paragraph (a) see Division 5. For paragraph (b) see section 187. For paragraph (c) see section 188. For paragraph (d) see sections 189 and 190.

section.heading: Voluntary surrender of retention licence

content.p: A retention licence holder may surrender the licence.
Note 1: See Division 4 for voluntary surrender of part of a licence area.
Note 2: The surrender takes effect when it is registered under section 337 (see subsection 337(5)).

section.heading: Automatic expiry of retention licence when mining licence takes effect

content.p: If:
a retention licence is in force under this Act; and
the Joint Authority provisionally grants a mining licence over all or some of the blocks in the retention licence area; and
the provisional grant of the mining licence is properly accepted; and
the grant of the mining licence comes into force;
the retention licence expires in relation to the blocks covered by the mining licence.

section.heading: Cancellation of retention licence—breach of condition etc.

content.p: Subject to subsection (5), the Joint Authority may cancel a retention licence if the licence holder:
breaches a licence condition; or
contravenes a provision of this Act or the regulations; or
breaches a condition attached to an approval under subsection 365(2); or
fails to pay user charge that is payable for the licence under the Retention Licence User Charge Act.
If the Joint Authority proposes to cancel a licence under subsection (1), the Designated Authority must give the holder a written notice that informs the holder of the proposed cancellation.
The notice must:
specify the reason for the proposed cancellation; and
invite the holder to make submissions in relation to the proposed cancellation; and
specify the day by which submissions should be given to the Joint Authority; and
specify an address where submissions are to be lodged.
The day specified under paragraph (3)(c) must be not less than 60 days after the day on which the notice is given.
The Joint Authority may cancel the licence only if:
the holder has been given a notice under subsection (2); and
the Joint Authority has considered:
any submission made by the holder; and
any steps taken by the holder to remedy the circumstances that led to the proposal to cancel the licence and to prevent those circumstances from happening again; and
the Joint Authority is satisfied that no special circumstances exist that justify the licence not being cancelled.

section.heading: Cancellation of retention licence—mining activities viable

content.p: If the Joint Authority believes that mining activities should commence in a retention licence area, the Designated Authority must ask the licence holder to explain why the holder should not apply for a mining licence over the retention licence area.
A request under subsection (1) must:
be in writing; and
specify the day by which the holder should give the explanation to the Designated Authority.
The day specified under paragraph (2)(b) is to be at least 30 days after the day on which the request is given to the holder.
An explanation provided in response to a request under subsection (1) must:
be in writing; and
be given to the Designated Authority.
The Joint Authority may cancel the retention licence if:
the holder is given a request under subsection (1); and
either:
the holder does not give the Designated Authority an explanation in response to the request by the day specified in the request; or
the holder gives the Designated Authority an explanation in response to the request but the Joint Authority does not consider the explanation to be satisfactory.
If the Joint Authority cancels a retention licence under subsection (5), the Joint Authority may specify the day on which the cancellation takes effect.

Without limiting subsection (6), the Joint Authority, in determining the day on which the cancellation is to take effect, may have regard to the time needed by the holder to obtain the grant of a mining licence over the retention licence area.

section.heading: Obligations of former retention licence holders and former associates

content.p: Subject to subsection (4), if:
a person was:
a retention licence holder; or
an associate of a retention licence holder; and
the licence:
expires; or
is cancelled; or
is surrendered; and
an obligation associated with the licence arising out of:
a licence condition; or
a direction given under section 387 by the Designated Authority in relation to the licence; or
this Act or the regulations;
has not been discharged; and
the person was bound by that obligation when the person was the licence holder or an associate;
the person remains bound by the obligation until the obligation is discharged.
Subsection (1) does not continue an obligation to carry out exploration or recovery activities.
Subsection (1) continues an obligation that a person had to carry out exploration or recovery activities in a particular manner if the person carries them out.
The Joint Authority may determine that the person is not subject to:
a particular obligation under this section; or
all the person’s remaining obligations under this section.
A determination under subsection (4) is to be in writing.

section.heading: Mining licences

content.p: This Part provides for the grant of mining licences over blocks in an offshore area.
A mining licence may be granted over:
a vacant standard block (see Division 2); or
certain blocks that are not vacant (see Division 2); or
a tender block (see Division 3).
Note 1: A tender block is a block that has been declared available for tender. A standard block is any other block (see sections 19 and 20).
Note 2: A retention or exploration licence holder may apply for a mining licence over the same area or part of the same area.

section.heading: Activities authorised by a mining licence

content.p: Subject to subsection (2), a mining licence holder may:
recover minerals in the licence area; and
explore for minerals in the licence area.
Note 1: Under subsection 23(1) the concept of exploration extends to activities that are directly related to exploration.
Note 2: Under subsection 24(1) the concept of recovery extends to activities that are directly related to the recovery of minerals.
If the licence is expressed to restrict the kind of minerals covered by the licence, the holder is not permitted to recover, or to explore for, minerals not covered by the licence.
A restriction on the kind of minerals covered by the licence may be inclusive (for example, only minerals A, B and C) or exclusive (for example, all minerals except A, B and C).
For the purposes of subsection (2), the holder does not recover an excluded mineral if, in the course of recovering, or exploring for, another mineral, the holder recovers some excluded mineral.

section.heading: Joint Authority may cancel or not renew mining licence without compensation

content.p: No compensation is payable because of the cancellation or non-renewal of a mining licence by the Joint Authority.
Note 1: The Joint Authority may cancel the licence under section 265.
Note 2: The Joint Authority may refuse under section 242 or 243 to renew the licence.

section.heading: Licence rights may be suspended

content.p: The Joint Authority must suspend particular rights conferred by a mining licence if the Joint Authority is satisfied that it is necessary in the national interest to do so.
The Joint Authority may suspend rights conferred under subsection (1) for a specified period or for an indefinite period.
The Joint Authority may end a suspension at any time.
A suspension or the ending of a suspension must be in writing.
If the Joint Authority:
suspends rights conferred by a mining licence; or
ends a suspension;
the Joint Authority must give the licence holder a written notice that informs the holder of the suspension or the ending of a suspension.
Note: See section 258 for the effect of the suspension on the obligations associated with the licence.
A suspension takes effect when:
the holder has been given notice of the suspension under subsection (5); and
the suspension has been registered under section 337.

section.heading: Compensation for acquisition of property due to suspension of rights

content.p: If:
the Joint Authority suspends licence rights under section 195; and
the suspension results in the acquisition of property from a person; and
the Commonwealth and the person agree on an amount of compensation for the acquisition;
the Commonwealth must pay the person the agreed amount of compensation.
If:
the Joint Authority suspends licence rights under section 195; and
the suspension results in the acquisition of property from a person; and
the Commonwealth and the person do not agree on an amount of compensation for the acquisition; and
the person brings an action for compensation against the Commonwealth in the High Court or an appropriate Supreme Court;
the Commonwealth must pay the person the amount of compensation (if any) that is determined by the court.
In this section:
acquisition of property means an acquisition of property within the meaning of paragraph 51(xxxi) of the Constitution.
appropriate Supreme Court means the Supreme Court of, or having jurisdiction in, the State or Territory for which the Joint Authority is established.

division.heading: Application for and grant of mining licence over standard blocks

section.heading: Application for mining licence over vacant standard block

content.p: A person may apply to the Joint Authority for a mining licence over a standard block that is vacant.
A standard block is vacant if no exploration, retention or mining licence is in force over the block.
The application must not cover more than 20 blocks.
If the application is for a licence over a group of blocks, the blocks must form a discrete area.

section.heading: Holder of exploration licence or retention licence may apply for mining licence

content.p: An exploration or retention licence holder may apply to the Joint Authority for a mining licence over all or some of the blocks in the licence area of the exploration or retention licence.
A person may apply for a mining licence under subsection (1) over a group of blocks only if:
the group forms a discrete area; and
there are not more than 20 blocks in the group.
The holder may apply for 2 or more mining licences over different parts of the licence area of the exploration or retention licence.

section.heading: How to apply

content.p: An application under section 197 or 198 must:
be made in accordance with the approved form; and
be made in the approved manner; and
specify the blocks for which the application is made; and
include details of:
the activities that the applicant intends to carry out on the block or blocks covered by the application; and
the amount of money that the applicant intends to spend on those activities; and
the technical qualifications of the applicant and of the applicant’s employees who are likely to be involved in activities authorised by the licence; and
the technical advice available to the applicant; and
the financial resources available to the applicant; and
if the licence is to be held by more than one person—the share of the licence that each prospective holder will hold; and
be accompanied by maps that:
relate to the blocks; and
comply with guidelines issued by the Designated Authority under subsection 41(2); and
specify an address for service of notices under this Act and the regulations.
Note: For paragraphs (a) and (b) see section 41.
The applicant may include in the application any other information that the applicant thinks is relevant.
