The application must be lodged with the Designated Authority.

section.heading: Effect of inclusion of unavailable block in application

content.p: If:
a person applies under section 197 or 198 for a licence over a group of blocks; and
because of section 18, 197 or 198:
a mining licence cannot be granted over one or more of the blocks in the group; or
the Joint Authority cannot grant the licence over one or more of the blocks in the group;
the Designated Authority and the Joint Authority may still deal with the application to the extent to which the application covers blocks:
for which a mining licence can be granted; or
for which the Joint Authority does have power to grant the licence applied for.
Note 1: A mining licence cannot be granted over a block that is not vacant or over a reserved block (see section 18).
Note 2: The Joint Authority for a State may grant a licence only over blocks in that State’s Commonwealth-State offshore area.

section.heading: Payment of fee

content.p: The applicant must pay the application fee prescribed by the regulations.
The fee must be paid when the application is made.
The Joint Authority may refund any fee paid under subsection (1) but only if it is satisfied that special circumstances exist that justify the refund of the fee.

section.heading: Application must be advertised

content.p: The applicant must advertise the application in a newspaper that circulates throughout the State or external territory concerned.
The advertisement must contain:
the applicant’s name and address; and
a map and description of the blocks applied for that are sufficient for the blocks to be identified; and
the address of the Designated Authority; and
a statement:
that the applicant has applied for a mining licence over the blocks described in the notice; and
that invites comment from the public on the application; and
that requests that comments be sent to the applicant and the Designated Authority within 30 days after the day on which the advertisement is published.
The advertisement must be published as soon as possible after the applicant applies for a mining licence.
Subject to subsection (5), the advertisement must be published within 14 days after the day on which the applicant lodges the application.
If:
the applicant applies to the Designated Authority within the 14 day period referred to in subsection (4) for an extension of the period; and
the Designated Authority extends the period;
the advertisement must be published within the period as extended by the Designated Authority.

section.heading: How multiple applications are dealt with

content.p: Subject to subsection (2), if a block is covered by 2 or more applications for a mining or exploration licence, the Designated Authority must deal with the applications in the order in which they are made.
Note: See also section 58.
If:
the applications are lodged within a particular time of each other; and
the time is less than the time prescribed by the regulations;
the Designated Authority must determine the order in which the applications are to be dealt with by drawing lots in the way prescribed by the regulations.

section.heading: Request for further information

content.p: The Designated Authority may ask the applicant for further information relating to the application.
The request must:
be in writing; and
be given to the applicant; and
specify the time within which the information must be provided.
Information requested under subsection (1) must be provided:
in writing; and
within the time specified in the request.

section.heading: Commonwealth-State offshore area—Designated Authority must refer application to Joint Authority if certain requirements met

content.p: This section applies if the application covers blocks in a Commonwealth-State offshore area.
If the applicant does what is required by sections 199 to 204, the Designated Authority must refer the application to the Joint Authority.
If the applicant does not do what is required by sections 199 to 204, the Designated Authority:
must not refer the application to the Joint Authority; and
must give the applicant written notice that the application has been refused.
The application lapses if a notice is given under subsection (3).

section.heading: Commonwealth-State offshore area—Joint Authority may provisionally grant mining licence

content.p: If the Designated Authority for a Commonwealth-State offshore area refers the application to the Joint Authority under section 205, the Joint Authority may:
provisionally grant a mining licence to the applicant; or
subject to section 208, refuse the application.

Note: Under section 232, the grant of the licence cannot be effective before it is registered (see section 333 for registration). The grant will not be registered until it has been properly accepted (see section 214 for proper acceptance).

section.heading: External territory offshore area—how application for mining licence dealt with

content.p: This section applies if the application covers blocks in an external territory offshore area.
If the applicant does not do what is required by sections 199 to 204, the responsible Commonwealth Minister (as the Joint Authority for that offshore area) must refuse the application.
If the applicant does what is required by sections 199 to 204, the responsible Commonwealth Minister (as the Joint Authority for that offshore area) may:
provisionally grant a mining licence to the applicant; or
subject to section 208, refuse the application.

Note: Under section 232, the grant of the licence cannot be effective before it is registered (see section 333 for registration). The grant will not be registered until it has been properly accepted (see section 214 for proper acceptance).

section.heading: Refusal of application for mining licence made under section 198

content.p: If the Joint Authority proposes to refuse an application for a mining licence made under section 198, the Designated Authority must notify the applicant of the proposed refusal.
The notice must:
be in writing; and
specify the reason for the proposed refusal; and
invite the applicant to make written submissions in relation to the proposed refusal; and
specify the day by which submissions should be given to the Designated Authority; and
specify an address where submissions are to be lodged.
The day specified under paragraph (2)(d) must be not less than 30 days after the day on which the notice is given.
The Joint Authority may refuse to grant an application for a mining licence made under section 198 only if:
the applicant has been given a notice under subsection (1); and
the Joint Authority has considered any submission made by the applicant; and
the Joint Authority is satisfied that no special circumstances exist that justify the licence being granted.

section.heading: Matters to be specified in the licence

content.p: The licence must specify:
the blocks covered by the licence; and
the term of the licence; and
the licence conditions.
The term specified under paragraph (1)(b) is not to exceed 21 years.

section.heading: Applicant must be notified

content.p: The Designated Authority must give the applicant written notice of the Joint Authority’s decision under section 206 or 207.
If the Joint Authority provisionally grants a mining licence:
the Designated Authority must give the licence to the provisional holder; and
the notice under subsection (1) must contain the following information:
notification of any determination under section 399 that the provisional holder must lodge a security;
notification that the provisional grant will lapse unless the provisional holder, before the end of the primary payment period:
(A) gives the Designated Authority a written acceptance of the grant; and
(B) lodges any security required by the Joint Authority under section 399; and
(C) pays the fees that must be paid for the licence under the Mining Licence Fees Act.

section.heading: Amendment of conditions

content.p: If the provisional holder is dissatisfied with a licence condition, the provisional holder may ask the Joint Authority to amend the condition.
The request must:
be made within 30 days after the day on which the provisional holder is given the licence under section 210; and
be lodged with the Designated Authority.
If the Joint Authority is given a request under subsection (1), the Joint Authority may amend the licence conditions.
The Designated Authority must give the provisional holder written notice of the amendment.

section.heading: Amendment of security requirements

content.p: If the provisional holder:
is notified of a security requirement; and
is dissatisfied with the amount of the security required;
the provisional holder may ask the Joint Authority to make a new determination under section 399.
The request must:
be made within 30 days after the day on which the applicant is given notice under section 210; and
be lodged with the Designated Authority.
If the Joint Authority is given a request under subsection (1), the Joint Authority may make a new determination under section 399.
The Designated Authority must give the provisional holder written notice of the new determination.

section.heading: Extension of primary payment period

content.p: If the provisional holder makes a request under section 211 or 212, the provisional holder may ask the Designated Authority to extend the primary payment period.
The request must be made within 30 days after the day on which the provisional holder is given notice under section 210.
If the Designated Authority agrees to the request, the Designated Authority must:
determine the period of the extension; and
give the provisional holder a written notice informing the applicant of the period of the extension.

section.heading: Acceptance of grant of mining licence for standard block

content.p: The provisional grant of a mining licence is properly accepted by the provisional holder if, before the end of the primary payment period, the provisional holder:
gives the Designated Authority a written acceptance of the grant; and
lodges any security required by the Joint Authority under section 399; and
pays the fees that must be paid for the licence under the Mining Licence Fees Act.
The provisional grant of a mining licence is properly accepted by the provisional holder if the provisional holder:
has been granted an extension of the primary payment period under section 213; and
before the end of the secondary payment period:
gives the Designated Authority a written acceptance of the grant; and
lodges any security required by the Joint Authority under section 399; and
pays the fees that must be paid for the licence under the Mining Licence Fees Act.
Note: Under section 232, the grant of the licence cannot be effective before it is registered (see section 333 for registration).

section.heading: Conditions applicable to licence on grant

content.p: If the provisional grant of the licence is properly accepted, it is subject to:
the conditions specified in the licence given to the applicant under section 210; or
if the Joint Authority amended those conditions under section 211—those conditions as amended.

section.heading: Lapse of provisional grant of mining licence

content.p: If the provisional grant of the licence is not properly accepted under section 214, the provisional grant lapses.

division.heading: Application for and grant of mining licence over tender block

section.heading: Matters to be determined before applications for mining licence over tender blocks invited

content.p: If the Joint Authority proposes to invite applications for the grant of a mining licence over reserved blocks, the Joint Authority must, before inviting the applications, determine:
the procedure and criteria that the Joint Authority will adopt to allocate the licence; and
the amount of security that will be required for the licence under section 399; and
the initial term of the licence; and
the licence conditions.
The term determined under paragraph (1)(c) is not to exceed 21 years.

section.heading: Joint Authority may invite applications for mining licence over tender blocks

content.p: Subject to subsection (2), the Joint Authority may invite applications for the grant of a mining licence over reserved blocks.
Applications may be invited for a licence covering a group of reserved blocks only if the group forms a discrete area.
The Joint Authority is to invite applications by publishing a tender block licence notice for the licence in the Gazette.
Note 1: A mining licence may cover not more than 20 tender blocks (see section 219).

Note 2: A mining licence might be made available by a tender block notice if a mineral deposit in the area had already been identified and sufficient information was already available to justify the issue of a mining licence rather than an exploration licence.

section.heading: Tender block licence notice—mining licence

content.p: A tender block licence notice for a mining licence must:
specify the blocks to be covered by the licence; and
specify the period within which applications may be made; and
specify the procedure and criteria that the Joint Authority will adopt to allocate the licence; and
specify the amount of security that the successful applicant will be required to lodge; and
specify the initial term of the licence; and
include a statement to the effect that information about:
the security that the successful applicant will be required to lodge; and
the licence conditions;
may be obtained from the Designated Authority.
The tender block licence notice may specify not more than 20 blocks for the mining licence.

section.heading: Application for mining licence over tender blocks

content.p: If a tender block licence notice has been published inviting applications for a mining licence, a person may apply for the licence.

section.heading: How to apply

content.p: The application must:
be made in accordance with the approved form; and
be made in the approved manner; and
be made before the end of the period specified in the tender block licence notice; and
include details of:
the technical qualifications of the applicant and of the applicant’s employees who are likely to be involved in activities authorised by the licence; and
the technical advice available to the applicant; and
the financial resources available to the applicant; and
if the licence is to be held by more than one person—the share of the licence that each prospective holder will hold; and
specify an address for service of notices under this Act and the regulations.
Note: For paragraphs (a) and (b) see section 41.

If the Joint Authority has specified in the tender block licence notice that it will select the successful applicant on the basis of development proposals submitted for the blocks to be covered by the licence, the application must include details of the applicant’s development proposals for the blocks.

If the Joint Authority has specified in the tender block licence notice that it will select the successful applicant on the basis of the amounts of money offered for the licence, the application must state the amount offered by the applicant for the licence.
The applicant may include in the application any other information that the applicant thinks is relevant.
The application must be lodged with the Designated Authority.

section.heading: Payment of fee

content.p: The applicant must pay the application fee prescribed by the regulations.
The fee must be paid when the application is made.
The Joint Authority may refund any fee paid under subsection (1) but only if it is satisfied that special circumstances exist that justify the refund of the fee.

section.heading: Request for further information

content.p: The Designated Authority may ask the applicant for further information relating to the application.
The request must:
be in writing; and
be given to the applicant; and
specify the time within which the information must be provided.
Information requested under subsection (1) must be provided:
in writing; and
within the time specified in the request.

section.heading: Commonwealth-State offshore area—Designated Authority must refer application to Joint Authority if certain requirements met

content.p: This section applies if the tender block notice relates to blocks in a Commonwealth-State offshore area.
If an applicant does what is required by sections 221 to 223, the Designated Authority must refer the application to the Joint Authority.
If an applicant does not do what is required by sections 221 to 223, the Designated Authority:
must not refer the application to the Joint Authority; and
must give the applicant written notice that the application has been refused.
The application lapses if a notice is given under subsection (3).

section.heading: Commonwealth-State offshore area—Joint Authority may provisionally grant tender block mining licence

content.p: If the Designated Authority refers applications to the Joint Authority under section 224, the Joint Authority may provisionally grant a mining licence to one of the applicants.

Note: Under section 232, the grant of the licence cannot be effective before it is registered (see section 333 for registration). The grant will not be registered until it has been properly accepted (see section 228 for proper acceptance).
The Joint Authority may provisionally grant a licence under subsection (1) even if only one application is referred to the Joint Authority by the Designated Authority.

When provisionally granting a licence under subsection (1), the Joint Authority must follow the procedure and apply the criteria specified in the tender block licence notice published for the licence under section 218.

section.heading: External territory offshore area—how applications dealt with

content.p: This section applies if the tender block licence notice relates to blocks in an external territory offshore area.
The responsible Commonwealth Minister (as the Joint Authority for that offshore area):
must refuse an application if the applicant does not do what is required by sections 221 to 223; and
may provisionally grant a mining licence to an applicant whose application has not been refused under paragraph (a).

Note: Under section 232, the grant of the licence cannot be effective before it is registered (see section 333 for registration). The grant will not be registered until it has been properly accepted (see section 228 for proper acceptance).
The responsible Commonwealth Minister may provisionally grant a licence under subsection (2) even if there is only one application that is not refused under paragraph (2)(a).

When provisionally granting a licence under subsection (2), the responsible Commonwealth Minister must follow the procedure and apply the criteria specified in the tender block licence notice published for the licence under section 218.

section.heading: Successful applicant must be notified

content.p: If the Joint Authority provisionally grants a mining licence under section 225, 226 or 231, the Designated Authority must give the provisional holder:
the licence; and
written notice that the provisional grant will lapse unless the provisional holder, before the end of the primary payment period:
gives the Designated Authority a written acceptance of the grant; and
lodges any security required by the Joint Authority under section 399; and
pays the fees that must be paid for the licence under the Mining Licence Fees Act; and
if the tender is determined on the basis of the amounts of money offered for the licence—pays the Commonwealth the amount that the provisional holder offered for the licence under subsection 221(3).
The licence must specify:
the blocks covered by the licence; and
the term of the licence; and
the licence conditions.
Note: For the term of a licence see subsection 217(2).

section.heading: Acceptance of grant of mining licence over tender blocks

content.p: The provisional grant of a mining licence is properly accepted by the provisional holder if, within 30 days after the day on which the provisional holder is given notice under section 227, the provisional holder:
gives the Designated Authority a written acceptance of the grant; and
lodges any security required by the Joint Authority under section 399; and
pays the fees that must be paid for the licence under the Mining Licence Fees Act; and
if the tender is determined on the basis of the amounts of money offered for the licence—pays the Commonwealth the amount that the provisional holder offered for the licence under subsection 221(3).
Note: Under section 232, the grant of the licence cannot be effective before it is registered (see section 333 for registration).

section.heading: Conditions applicable to licence on grant

content.p: If the provisional grant of the licence is properly accepted, the licence is subject to the conditions determined under section 217.

section.heading: Lapse of provisional grant of mining licence

content.p: If the provisional grant of the licence is not properly accepted under section 229, the provisional grant lapses.

section.heading: Provisional grant to next applicant if grant lapses

content.p: If the provisional grant of the licence lapses under section 230, the Joint Authority may provisionally grant the licence to another of the applicants for the licence.

When provisionally granting a licence under subsection (1), the Joint Authority must follow the procedure and apply the criteria specified in the tender block licence notice published for the licence under section 218.

section.heading: Initial term of mining licence

content.p: A mining licence comes into force on:
the day on which the grant of the licence is registered; or
if a day later than the day on which the grant of the licence is registered is specified in the licence as its commencement day—that specified day.
The initial term of a mining licence ends:
if the licence is granted under Division 2—at the end of the period specified in the licence under subsection 209(1); or
if the licence is granted under Division 3—at the end of the period specified under subsection 227(2).
Note 1: For the maximum initial term of renewal see subsections 209(2) and 217(2).
Note 2: The licence may be surrendered at any time (see section 264).
The period runs from:
the day on which the licence is provisionally granted; or
if a day later than the day on which the licence is provisionally granted is specified in the licence as its commencement day—that specified day.

section.heading: Term of renewal of licence

content.p: A renewal of a mining licence comes into force on:
the day on which the renewal is registered; or
the day on which the previous term of the licence expires;
whichever is the later.
Note: See Division 6 for renewal.
The term of a renewal of a licence ends at the end of the period specified in the notice under section 246.
Note 1: For the maximum term of renewal see subsection 246(3).
Note 2: The licence may be surrendered at any time (see section 264).
The period runs from the day on which the previous term of the licence expires.
Ignore section 234 in working out the period referred to in subsection (3).

section.heading: Effect of application for renewal on term of mining licence

content.p: If:
a mining licence holder applies to renew the licence under section 236; and
the current term of the licence expires; and
a renewal of the licence does not take effect immediately after the current term expires;
the licence remains in force after the current term expires until:
a renewal of the licence takes effect; or
a provisional renewal of the licence lapses; or
the application for renewal is withdrawn or refused.

division.heading: Voluntary surrender of part of mining licence area

section.heading: Voluntary surrender of blocks if discrete area remains

content.p: A mining licence holder may surrender a block or some of the blocks covered by the licence if the remaining blocks in the licence area form a discrete area.
Note: See section 264 for the surrender of the whole licence.
A surrender under subsection (1) must:
be made in writing; and
identify the blocks surrendered; and
be given to the Designated Authority.
Note: The surrender takes effect when it is registered under section 337 (see subsection 337(5)).

division.heading: Application for and grant of renewal of mining licence

section.heading: Application for renewal of mining licence

content.p: A mining licence holder may apply to the Joint Authority to renew the licence.
Note: At each renewal, the licence conditions are reviewed (see section 254).

section.heading: When must an application to renew be made?

content.p: Subject to this section, the application must be made at least 6 months before the day on which the licence is to expire.
The Designated Authority may accept an application that is made later than 6 months before the day on which the licence is to expire if:
the application is made before the day on which the licence expires; and
the Designated Authority believes that there are reasonable grounds for accepting the application.

section.heading: How to apply for renewal

content.p: The application must:
be made in accordance with the approved form; and
be made in the approved manner; and
include details of:
the activities carried out by the applicant under the licence during its current term; and
the amount of money spent by the applicant in relation to the blocks covered by the licence during its current term; and
the activities that the applicant intends to carry out under the licence during the term applied for; and
the amount of money that the applicant intends to spend in relation to activities authorised by the licence during the term applied for.
Note: For paragraphs (a) and (b) see section 41.
The applicant may include in the application any other information that the applicant thinks is relevant.
The application must be lodged with the Designated Authority.

section.heading: Request for further information

content.p: The Designated Authority may ask the applicant to provide further information relating to the application.
The request must:
be in writing; and
be given to the applicant; and
specify the time within which the information must be provided.
Information requested under subsection (1) must be provided:
in writing; and
within the time specified in the request.

section.heading: Payment of fee

content.p: The applicant must pay the application fee prescribed by the regulations.
The fee must be paid when the application is made.
The Joint Authority may refund any fee paid under subsection (1) but only if it is satisfied that special circumstances exist that justify the refund of the fee.

section.heading: Commonwealth-State offshore area—Designated Authority must refer renewal application to Joint Authority if certain requirements met

content.p: This section applies if the renewal application covers blocks in a Commonwealth-State offshore area.
If the applicant does what is required by sections 237 to 240, the Designated Authority must refer the application to the Joint Authority.
If the applicant does not do what is required by sections 237 to 240, the Designated Authority:
must not refer the application to the Joint Authority; and
must give the applicant written notice that the application has been refused.
The application lapses if a notice is given under subsection (3).

section.heading: Commonwealth-State offshore area—provisional renewal of mining licence

content.p: If the Designated Authority for a Commonwealth-State offshore area refers the renewal application to the Joint Authority under section 241, the Joint Authority may:
provisionally renew the licence; or
subject to section 245, refuse to renew the licence.

Note 1: Under section 233, the renewal of the licence cannot be effective before it is registered (see section 334 for registration). The renewal will not be registered until it has been properly accepted (see section 250 for proper acceptance).
Note 2: Under section 254, new conditions may be imposed on renewal.

section.heading: External territory offshore area—how application for renewal dealt with

content.p: This section applies if the renewal application covers blocks in an external territory offshore area.
If the applicant does not do what is required by sections 237 to 240, the responsible Commonwealth Minister (as the Joint Authority for the offshore area) must refuse to renew the licence.
If the applicant does what is required by sections 237 to 240, the responsible Commonwealth Minister (as the Joint Authority for that offshore area) may:
provisionally renew the licence; or
subject to section 245, refuse to renew the licence.

Note 1: Under section 233, the renewal of the licence cannot be effective before it is registered (see section 334 for registration). The renewal will not be registered until it has been properly accepted (see section 250 for proper acceptance).
Note 2: Under section 254, new conditions may be imposed on renewal.

section.heading: Matters to be taken into account in deciding whether to renew mining licence

content.p: In deciding whether to renew a mining licence, the Joint Authority may have regard to whether the applicant has complied with:
this Act; and
the regulations; and
any licence conditions.

section.heading: Refusal of application for renewal

content.p: If the Joint Authority proposes to refuse to renew the licence, the Designated Authority must give the applicant notice of the proposed refusal.
The notice must:
be in writing; and
specify the reason for the proposed refusal; and
invite the holder to make written submissions in relation to the proposed refusal; and
specify the day by which submissions should be given to the Designated Authority; and
specify an address where submissions are to be lodged.
The day specified under paragraph (2)(d) must be not less than 30 days after the day on which the notice is given.
The Joint Authority may refuse to grant the application only if:
the holder has been given a notice under subsection (1); and
the Joint Authority has considered any submission made by the applicant; and
the Joint Authority is satisfied that no special circumstances exist that justify the renewal being granted.

section.heading: Applicant must be notified

content.p: The Designated Authority must give the applicant written notice of the Joint Authority’s decision under section 242 or 243.
If the Joint Authority provisionally renews the licence under section 242 or 243, the notice must contain the following information:
notification of the term of the renewal;
notification of the conditions of the renewed licence;
notification of any determination under section 399 that the applicant must lodge a security or a further security;
notification that the provisional renewal will lapse unless the applicant, before the end of the primary payment period:
gives the Designated Authority a written acceptance of the renewal; and
lodges any security required by the Joint Authority under section 399; and
pays the fees that must be paid for the renewal under the Mining Licence Fees Act.
Note: Section 254 provides for renewals to be granted subject to conditions.
The term specified under paragraph (2)(a) is not to be more than 21 years.

section.heading: Amendment of conditions

content.p: If the licence holder:
has been provisionally granted a renewal of the licence under section 242 or 243; and
is notified of the licence conditions; and
is dissatisfied with a condition;
the holder may ask the Joint Authority to amend the condition.
The request must:
be made within 30 days after the day on which the holder is given notice under section 246; and
be lodged with the Designated Authority.
If the Joint Authority is given a request under subsection (1), the Joint Authority may amend the licence conditions.
The Designated Authority must give the holder written notice of the amendment.

section.heading: Amendment of security requirements

content.p: If the licence holder:
has been provisionally granted a renewal of the licence under section 242 or 243; and
is notified of a security requirement for the licence; and
is dissatisfied with the amount of the security required;
the holder may ask the Joint Authority to make a new determination under section 399.
The request must:
be made within 30 days after the day on which the holder is given notice under section 246; and
be lodged with the Designated Authority.
If the Joint Authority is given a request under subsection (1), the Authority may make a new determination under section 399.
The Designated Authority must give the holder written notice of the new determination.

section.heading: Extension of primary payment period

content.p: If the licence holder makes a request under section 247 or 248, the holder may ask the Designated Authority to extend the primary payment period.
The request must be made within 30 days after the day on which the holder is given notice under section 246.
If the Designated Authority agrees to the request, the Designated Authority must:
determine the period of the extension in writing; and
give the holder a written notice informing the holder of the period of the extension.

section.heading: Acceptance of renewal of mining licence

content.p: The provisional renewal of a mining licence is properly accepted by the licence holder if, before the end of the primary payment period, the holder:
gives the Designated Authority a written acceptance of the renewal; and
lodges any security required by the Joint Authority under section 399; and
pays the fees that must be paid under the Mining Licence Fees Act.
Note: Under section 233, the renewal of the licence cannot be effective before it is registered (see section 334 for registration).
The provisional renewal of a mining licence is properly accepted by the licence holder if the holder:
has been granted an extension of the primary payment period under section 249; and
before the end of the secondary payment period:
gives the Designated Authority a written acceptance of the renewal; and
lodges any security required by the Joint Authority under section 399; and
pays the fees that must be paid under the Mining Licence Fees Act.
Note: Under section 233, the renewal of the licence cannot be effective before it is registered (see section 334 for registration).

section.heading: Conditions applicable to licence on renewal

content.p: If the provisional renewal is properly accepted, the renewed licence is subject to:
the conditions specified in the notice given to the licence holder under section 246; or
if the Joint Authority amended those conditions under section 247—those conditions as amended.

section.heading: Lapse of provisional renewal of mining licence

content.p: If the provisional renewal of a mining licence is not properly accepted under section 250, the provisional renewal lapses.

section.heading: General

content.p: The sources of obligations associated with a mining licence are:
the licence conditions; and
obligations arising from compliance directions given by the Designated Authority; and
obligations imposed by this Act and the regulations.
Note: For paragraph (a) see sections 254 to 256. For paragraph (b) see section 387. For paragraph (c) see sections 259 to 262 and section 372.
If a mining licence has 2 or more holders, all the holders are jointly and severally bound by the obligations that attach to the licence.

section.heading: Conditions of mining licence

content.p: The Joint Authority may grant or renew a mining licence subject to whatever conditions the Joint Authority thinks appropriate.
If the Joint Authority grants or renews a mining licence subject to conditions, the conditions must be specified in the licence.
Without limiting subsection (1), the Joint Authority may attach the following kinds of conditions to the grant or renewal of a mining licence:
a condition requiring the licence holder to take out insurance as required by the Designated Authority;

a condition requiring the holder to carry out certain work in or in relation to the licence area during the term of the licence, and to comply with directions concerning that work given under section 387;
a condition requiring the holder to lodge a security with the Designated Authority;
a condition requiring the holder to keep specified information;
a condition requiring the holder to give to the Designated Authority, on request, specified information;
a condition requiring the holder to take steps to protect the environment of the licence area, including conditions relating to:
protecting wildlife; or
minimising the effect on the environment of the licence area and the area surrounding the licence area of activities carried out in the licence area;
a condition requiring the holder to repair any damage to the environment caused by activities in the licence area;
a condition requiring the holder to pay a specified penalty to the Commonwealth if the holder does not comply with a licence condition.
A condition under paragraph (3)(c) must specify:
the amount of the security required; and
the kind of security required; and
the manner and form in which the security is to be lodged.
Without limiting paragraph (3)(c), a condition under that paragraph may require the lodgment of a security in the form of a guarantee and if a guarantee is required the condition may specify:
the kind of person who is to give the guarantee; and
the terms of the guarantee.

section.heading: No conditions requiring payment of money

content.p: Except for a condition requiring the payment of a penalty or lodgment of security, a licence condition must not require the payment of money to:
the Designated Authority; or
the Joint Authority; or
the Commonwealth.

section.heading: Variation of conditions

content.p: If:
a mining licence holder requests the Designated Authority in writing to vary a licence condition; or
part of the licence area of a mining licence is surrendered under section 235;
a Joint Authority may vary a licence condition.
If a Designated Authority gives:
a direction under section 387; or
an approval, consent or exemption under the regulations;

to a mining licence holder, the Joint Authority may vary a licence condition to the extent necessary to avoid inconsistency between the licence conditions and the direction, approval, consent or exemption.
The Joint Authority may vary a licence condition subject to whatever conditions the Joint Authority thinks appropriate.
If the Joint Authority varies a licence condition, the Designated Authority must give the licence holder a written notice that:
informs the holder of the variation; and
specifies the conditions which have been varied; and
specifies any conditions to which the variation is subject.

section.heading: Exemption from or suspension of conditions

content.p: If:
a mining licence holder requests the Designated Authority in writing to:
suspend a licence condition; or
exempt the holder from complying with a licence condition; or
part of the licence area of a mining licence is surrendered under section 235;
the Joint Authority may:
suspend a licence condition; or
exempt the holder from complying with a licence condition.
If a Designated Authority gives:
a direction under section 387; or
an approval, consent or exemption under the regulations;

to a mining licence holder, the Joint Authority may suspend a licence condition, or exempt the holder from compliance with a licence condition, to the extent necessary to avoid inconsistency between the licence conditions and the direction, approval, consent or exemption.
The Joint Authority may:
suspend a licence condition; or
exempt the licence holder from complying with a licence condition;
subject to whatever conditions the Joint Authority thinks appropriate.
If the Joint Authority:
suspends a licence condition; or
exempts the licence holder from complying with a licence condition;
the Designated Authority must give the holder a written notice that:
informs the holder of the exemption or suspension; and
specifies the conditions which have been suspended or affected by the exemption; and
specifies any conditions to which the suspension or exemption is subject.
Note: A suspension or exemption of a condition does not take effect until registered (see section 337).

section.heading: Automatic suspension of conditions if licence rights are suspended

content.p: If:
the Joint Authority suspends particular rights conferred by a mining licence under section 195; and
a licence condition is affected by the suspension;
the licence condition is suspended for the period of the suspension of the rights.

section.heading: Work practices

content.p: If a person who is:
a mining licence holder; or
an associate of the holder;
carries out activities in the licence area that are authorised by the licence, the person must take all reasonable steps:
to ensure that the activities are carried out at a standard that is accepted as reasonable and proper in the mining industry; and
to protect the health, safety and welfare of people engaged in the activities in and about the licence area; and
to maintain in good repair all structures and equipment in the licence area brought there by the person; and
to remove from the licence area any structure, equipment or other property that:
belongs to the person, or is under the person’s control; and
is not being used, or is not going to be used, in connection with the activities.
Penalty: 200 penalty units.

section.heading: Licence holder must comply with Royalty Act

content.p: A mining licence holder must comply with the Royalty Act.

section.heading: Licence holder must keep specified records

content.p: A mining licence holder must:
keep whatever records, cores and samples; and
give whatever records, cores and samples to the Designated Authority for inspection; and
make whatever returns;
are necessary to comply with:
the regulations; or
the licence conditions; or
a direction given by the Designated Authority under section 387.
Note: Under section 387 the Designated Authority may direct a person to keep records and cores, to collect and retain samples, and to make returns.
Penalty: 100 penalty units.

section.heading: Licence holder must assist inspectors

content.p: A mining licence holder must provide an inspector with reasonable facilities and assistance so that the inspector is able to carry out compliance inspections.
Note: See sections 377 to 384 for compliance inspections.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: General

content.p: A mining licence expires if:
the term of the licence expires without the licence being renewed; or
the licence holder surrenders the licence; or
the licence is cancelled.
Note: For paragraph (a) see Division 6. For paragraph (b) see section 264. For paragraph (c) see section 265.

section.heading: Voluntary surrender of mining licence

content.p: A mining licence holder may surrender the licence.
Note 1: See Division 5 for voluntary surrender of part of a licence area.
Note 2: The surrender takes effect when it is registered under section 337 (see subsection 337(5)).

section.heading: Cancellation of mining licence

content.p: Subject to subsection (5), the Joint Authority may cancel a mining licence if the licence holder:
breaches a licence condition; or
contravenes a provision of this Act or the regulations; or
breaches a condition attached to an approval under subsection 365(2).
If the Joint Authority proposes to cancel a licence under subsection (1), the Designated Authority must give the licence holder a written notice that informs the holder of the proposed cancellation.
The notice must:
specify the reason for the proposed cancellation; and
invite the holder to make submissions in relation to the proposed cancellation; and
specify the day by which submissions should be given to the Joint Authority; and
specify an address where submissions are to be lodged.
The day specified under paragraph (3)(c) must be not less than 60 days after the day on which the notice is given.
The Joint Authority may cancel the licence only if:
the holder has been given a notice under subsection (2); and
the Joint Authority has considered:
any submission made by the holder; and
any steps taken by the holder to remedy the circumstances that led to the proposal to cancel the licence and to prevent those circumstances from happening again; and
the Joint Authority is satisfied that no special circumstances exist that justify the licence not being cancelled.

section.heading: Obligations of former mining licence holders and former associates

content.p: Subject to subsection (4), if:
a person was:
a mining licence holder; or
an associate of a mining licence holder; and
the licence:
expires; or
is cancelled; or
is surrendered; and
an obligation associated with the licence arising out of:
a licence condition; or
a direction given under section 387 by the Designated Authority in relation to the licence; or
this Act or the regulations;
has not been discharged; and
the person was bound by that obligation when the person was the licence holder or an associate;
the person remains bound by the obligation until the obligation is discharged.
Subsection (1) does not continue an obligation to carry out exploration or recovery activities.
Subsection (1) continues an obligation that a person had to carry out exploration or recovery activities in a particular manner if the person carries them out.
The Joint Authority may determine that the person is not subject to:
a particular obligation under this section; or
all the person’s remaining obligations under this section.
A determination under subsection (4) is to be in writing.

section.heading: Works licences

content.p: This Part provides for the grant of works licences over blocks in an offshore area.
Note: A works licence allows licence-related activities to be carried out on blocks that are outside the licence area of the exploration, retention or mining licence concerned.
A works licence can only authorise activities that:
are directly connected with activities that are carried out, or are to be carried out, under an exploration, retention or mining licence; and
are necessary or desirable for the exploration, retention or mining licence holder to:
effectively exercise the licence rights; or
effectively perform the licence obligations.
A works licence can be granted over a particular block even though the block is a reserved block or is in someone else’s licence area.
More than one works licence can be granted over a particular block.
A works licence may be granted so as to allow activities that are connected with 2 or more licences.

section.heading: Activities authorised by a works licence

content.p: A works licence holder may carry out in the licence area the activities that are specified in the licence.

section.heading: Joint Authority may cancel or not renew works licence without compensation

content.p: No compensation is payable because of the cancellation or non-renewal of a works licence by the Joint Authority.
Note 1: The Joint Authority may cancel the licence under section 313.
Note 2: The Joint Authority may refuse under section 294 or 295 to renew the licence.

division.heading: Application for and grant of works licence

section.heading: Application for works licence

content.p: A person may apply to the Joint Authority for a works licence over a block.

section.heading: How to apply

content.p: The application must:
be made in accordance with the approved form; and
be made in the approved manner; and
include details of the activities that the applicant proposes to carry out; and
be accompanied by a map that shows the proposed location of the activities; and
specify an address for service of notices under this Act and the regulations.
Note: For paragraphs (a) and (b) see section 41.
The applicant may include in the application any other information that the applicant thinks is relevant.
The application must be lodged with the Designated Authority.

section.heading: Payment of fee

content.p: The applicant must pay the application fee prescribed by the regulations.
The fee must be paid when the application is made.
The Joint Authority may refund any fee paid under subsection (1) but only if it is satisfied that special circumstances exist that justify the refund of the fee.

section.heading: Applicant to notify licence holders affected by the application

content.p: The applicant must notify interested licence holders of the application.
The notification:
must be given to the interested licence holder in writing; and
must give details of the works licence applied for; and
must invite the interested licence holder to give comments to the Designated Authority within 30 days after the day on which the notice is given.
For the purposes of this section, a licence holder is interested if:
a block covered by the application is inside the licence area; and
the holder is not the applicant.

section.heading: Application must be advertised

content.p: The applicant must advertise the application in a newspaper circulating throughout the State or external territory concerned.
The advertisement must contain:
the applicant’s name and address; and
a map and description of the blocks covered that are sufficient for the blocks to be identified; and
details of the activities that the applicant proposes to carry out; and
a map showing the proposed location of those activities; and
the address of the Designated Authority; and
a statement:
that the applicant has applied for a works licence over the blocks described in the notice; and
that invites comment from the public on the application; and
that requests that comments be sent to the applicant and to the Designated Authority specified in the notice within 30 days of the day on which the advertisement is published.
The advertisement must be published as soon as possible after the applicant applies for the works licence.
Subject to subsection (5), the advertisement must be published within 14 days after the day on which the applicant lodges the application.
If:
the applicant applies to the Designated Authority within the 14 day period referred to in subsection (4) for an extension of the period; and
the Designated Authority extends the period;
the advertisement must be published within the period as extended by the Designated Authority.

section.heading: Commonwealth-State offshore area—Designated Authority must refer application to Joint Authority if certain requirements met

content.p: This section applies if the application covers blocks in a Commonwealth-State offshore area.
If the applicant does what is required by sections 271 to 274, the Designated Authority must refer the application to the Joint Authority.
If the applicant does not do what is required by sections 271 to 274, the Designated Authority:
must not refer the application to the Joint Authority; and
must give the applicant written notice that the application has been refused.
The application lapses if a notice is given under subsection (3).

section.heading: Commonwealth-State offshore area—Joint Authority may provisionally grant works licence

content.p: If the Designated Authority for a Commonwealth-State offshore area refers the application to the Joint Authority under section 275, the Joint Authority may:
provisionally grant a works licence to the applicant; or
refuse the application.

Note: Under section 286, the grant of the licence cannot be effective before it is registered (see section 333 for registration). The grant will not be registered until it has been properly accepted (see section 283 for proper acceptance).

section.heading: External territory offshore area—how application for works licence dealt with

content.p: This section applies if the application covers blocks in an external territory offshore area.
If the applicant does not do what is required by sections 271 to 274, the responsible Commonwealth Minister (as the Joint Authority for that offshore area) must refuse the application.
If the applicant does what is required by sections 271 to 274, the responsible Commonwealth Minister (as the Joint Authority for that offshore area) may:
provisionally grant a works licence to the applicant; or
refuse the application.

Note: Under section 286, the grant of the licence cannot be effective before it is registered (see section 333 for registration). The grant will not be registered until it has been properly accepted (see section 283 for proper acceptance).

section.heading: Matters to be specified in the licence

content.p: The licence must specify:
the blocks covered by the licence; and
the activities authorised by the licence; and
the area in which the activities are to be carried out; and
the term of the licence; and
the licence conditions.
The term specified under paragraph (1)(d) is not to exceed 5 years.

section.heading: Applicant must be notified

content.p: The Designated Authority must give the applicant written notice of the Joint Authority’s decision under section 276 or 277.
If the Joint Authority provisionally grants a works licence:
the Designated Authority must give the licence to the provisional holder; and
the notice under subsection (1) must contain the following information:
notification of any determination under section 399 that the provisional holder must lodge a security;
notification that the provisional grant will lapse unless the provisional holder, before the end of the primary payment period:
(A) gives the Designated Authority a written acceptance of the grant; and
(B) lodges any security required by the Joint Authority under section 399; and
(C) pays the fees that must be paid for the licence under the Works Licence Fees Act.

section.heading: Amendment of conditions

content.p: If the provisional holder is dissatisfied with a licence condition, the provisional holder may ask the Joint Authority to amend the condition.
The request must:
be made within 30 days after the day on which the provisional holder is given the licence under section 279; and
be lodged with the Designated Authority.
If the Joint Authority receives a request under subsection (1), the Joint Authority may amend the licence conditions.
The Designated Authority must give the provisional holder written notice of the amendment.

section.heading: Amendment of security requirements

content.p: If the provisional holder:
is notified of a security requirement; and
is dissatisfied with the amount of the security required;
the provisional holder may ask the Joint Authority to make a new determination under section 399.
The request must:
be made within 30 days after the day on which the applicant is given notice under section 279; and
be lodged with the Designated Authority.
If the Joint Authority receives a request under subsection (1), the Joint Authority may make a new determination under section 399.
The Designated Authority must give the provisional holder written notice of the new determination.

section.heading: Extension of primary payment period

content.p: If the provisional holder makes a request under section 280 or 281, the provisional holder may ask the Designated Authority to extend the primary payment period.
The request must be made within 30 days after the day on which the provisional holder is given notice under section 279.
If the Designated Authority agrees to the request, the Designated Authority must:
determine the period of the extension; and
give the provisional holder a written notice informing the holder of the period of the extension.

section.heading: Acceptance of grant of works licence

content.p: The provisional grant of a works licence is properly accepted by the provisional holder if, before the end of the primary payment period, the provisional holder:
gives the Designated Authority a written acceptance of the grant; and
lodges any security required by the Joint Authority under section 399; and
pays the fees that must be paid for the licence under the Works Licence Fees Act.
Note: Under section 286, the grant of the licence cannot be effective before it is registered (see section 333 for registration).
The provisional grant of a works licence is properly accepted by the provisional holder if the provisional holder:
has been granted an extension of the primary payment period under section 282; and
before the end of the secondary payment period:
gives the Designated Authority a written acceptance of the grant; and
lodges any security required by the Joint Authority under section 399; and
pays the fees that must be paid for the licence under the Works Licence Fees Act.
Note: Under section 286, the grant of the licence cannot be effective before it is registered (see section 333 for registration).

section.heading: Conditions applicable to works licence on grant

content.p: If the provisional grant of the licence is properly accepted, it is subject to:
the conditions specified in the licence given to the applicant under section 279; or
if the Joint Authority amended those conditions under section 280—those conditions as amended.

section.heading: Lapse of provisional grant of works licence

content.p: If the provisional grant of the licence is not properly accepted under section 283, the provisional grant lapses.

section.heading: Initial term of works licence

content.p: A works licence comes into force on:
the day on which the grant of the licence is registered; or
if a day later than the day on which the grant of the licence is registered is specified in the licence as its commencement day—that specified day.
The initial term of a works licence expires at the end of the period specified in the licence under subsection 278(1).
Note 1: For the maximum initial term see subsection 278(2).
Note 2: The licence may be surrendered at any time (see section 312).
The period is to run from:
the day on which the licence is provisionally granted; or
if a day later than the day on which the licence is provisionally granted is specified in the licence as the licence’s commencement day—that specified day.

section.heading: Term of renewal of works licence

content.p: A renewal of a works licence comes into force on:
the day on which the renewal is registered; or
the day on which the previous term of the licence expires;
whichever is the later.
Note: See Division 4 for renewal.
The term of a renewal of a licence expires at the end of the period specified in the notice under section 296.
Note 1: For the maximum term of renewal see subsection 296(3).
Note 2: The licence may be surrendered at any time (see section 312).
The period runs from the day on which the previous term of the licence expires.

section.heading: Effect of application for renewal on term of works licence

content.p: If:
a works licence holder applies to renew the licence under section 289; and
the current term of the licence expires; and
a renewal of the licence does not take effect immediately after the current term expires;
the licence remains in force after the current term expires until:
a renewal of the licence takes effect; or
a provisional renewal of the licence lapses; or
the application for renewal is withdrawn or refused;
whichever happens first.

division.heading: Application for and grant of renewal of works licence

section.heading: Application for renewal of works licence

content.p: A works licence holder may apply to the Joint Authority to renew the licence.
Note: At each renewal, the works licence conditions are reviewed (see section 304).

section.heading: When must an application to renew be made?

content.p: Subject to subsection (2), the application must be made at least 30 days before the day on which the licence is to expire.
The Designated Authority may accept an application that is made later than 30 days before the day on which the works licence is to expire if:
the application is made before the day on which the licence expires; and
the Designated Authority believes that there are reasonable grounds for accepting the application.

section.heading: How to apply for renewal

content.p: The application must:
be made in accordance with the approved form; and
be made in the approved manner; and
include details of:
the activities carried out by the applicant under the licence during its current term; and
the amount of money spent by the applicant in relation to the blocks covered by the licence during its current term; and
the activities that the applicant intends to carry out under the licence during the term applied for; and
the amount of money that the applicant intends to spend in relation to the activities authorised by the licence during the term applied for.
Note: For paragraphs (a) and (b) see section 41.
The applicant may include in the application any other information that the applicant thinks is relevant.
The application must be lodged with the Designated Authority.

section.heading: Payment of fee

content.p: The applicant must pay the application fee prescribed by the regulations.
The fee must be paid when the application is made.
The Joint Authority may refund any fee paid under subsection (1) but only if it is satisfied that special circumstances exist that justify the refund of the fee.

section.heading: Commonwealth-State offshore area—Designated Authority must refer renewal application to Joint Authority if certain requirements met

content.p: This section applies if the renewal application covers blocks in a Commonwealth-State offshore area.
If the applicant does what is required by sections 290 to 292, the Designated Authority must refer the application to the Joint Authority.
If the applicant does not do what is required by sections 290 to 292, the Designated Authority:
must not refer the application to the Joint Authority; and
must give the applicant written notice that the application has been refused.
The application lapses if a notice is given under subsection (3).

section.heading: Commonwealth-State offshore area—provisional renewal of works licence

content.p: If the Designated Authority for a Commonwealth-State offshore area refers the application to the Joint Authority under section 293, the Joint Authority may:
provisionally renew the licence; or
refuse to renew the licence.

Note 1: Under section 287, the renewal of the licence cannot be effective before it is registered (see section 334 for registration). The renewal will not be registered until it has been properly accepted (see section 300 for proper acceptance).
Note 2: Under section 304, new conditions may be imposed on renewal.

section.heading: External territory offshore area—how application for renewal dealt with

content.p: This section applies if the renewal application covers blocks in an external territory offshore area.
If the applicant does not do what is required by sections 290 to 292, the responsible Commonwealth Minister (as the Joint Authority for the offshore area) must refuse to renew the licence.
If the applicant does what is required by sections 290 to 292, the responsible Commonwealth Minister (as the Joint Authority for that offshore area) may:
provisionally renew the licence; or
refuse to renew the licence.

Note 1: Under section 287, the renewal of the licence cannot be effective before it is registered (see section 334 for registration). The renewal will not be registered until it has been properly accepted (see section 300 for proper acceptance).
Note 2: Under section 304, new conditions may be imposed on renewal.

section.heading: Applicant must be notified

content.p: The Designated Authority must give the applicant written notice of the Joint Authority’s decision under section 294 or 295.
If the Joint Authority provisionally renews the works licence under section 294 or 295, the notice must contain the following information:
notification of the term of the renewal;
notification of the conditions of the renewed licence;
notification that the provisional renewal will lapse unless the applicant, before the end of the primary payment period:
gives the Designated Authority a written acceptance of the renewal; and
lodges any security required by the Joint Authority under section 399; and
pays the fees that must be paid under the Works Licence Fees Act.
Note: Paragraph (b): section 304 provides for renewals to be granted subject to conditions.
The term specified under paragraph (2)(a) is not to be more than 5 years.

section.heading: Amendment of conditions

content.p: If the licence holder:
has been provisionally granted a renewal of the licence under section 294 or 295; and
is notified of the licence conditions; and
is dissatisfied with a licence condition;
the holder may ask the Joint Authority to amend the condition.
The request must:
be made within 30 days after the day on which the holder is given notice under section 296; and
be lodged with the Designated Authority.
If the Joint Authority is given a request under subsection (1), the Joint Authority may amend the licence conditions.
The Designated Authority must give the holder written notice of the amendment.

section.heading: Amendment of security requirements

content.p: If the licence holder:
has been provisionally granted a renewal of the licence under section 294 or 295; and
is notified of a security requirement; and
is dissatisfied with the amount of security required;
the holder may ask the Joint Authority to make a new determination under section 399.
The request must:
be made within 30 days after the day on which the holder is given notice under section 296; and
be lodged with the Designated Authority.
If the Joint Authority is given a request under subsection (1), the Authority may make a new determination under section 399.
The Designated Authority must give the holder written notice of the new determination.

section.heading: Extension of primary payment period

content.p: If the licence holder makes a request under section 297 or 298, the holder may ask the Designated Authority to extend the primary payment period.
The request must be made within 30 days after the day on which the holder is given notice under section 296.
If the Designated Authority agrees to the request, the Designated Authority must:
determine the period of the extension in writing; and
give the holder written notice informing the holder of the period of the extension.

section.heading: Acceptance of renewal of works licence

content.p: The provisional renewal of a works licence is properly accepted by the holder if, before the end of the primary payment period, the holder:
gives the Designated Authority a written acceptance of the renewal; and
lodges any security required by the Joint Authority under section 399; and
pays the fees that must be paid under the Works Licence Fees Act.
Note: Under section 287, the renewal of the licence cannot be effective before it is registered (see section 334 for registration).
The provisional renewal of a works licence is properly accepted by the holder if the holder:
has been granted an extension of the primary payment period under section 299; and
before the end of the secondary payment period:
gives the Designated Authority a written acceptance of the renewal; and
lodges any security required by the Joint Authority under section 399; and
pays the fees that must be paid under the Works Licence Fees Act.
Note: Under section 287, the renewal of the licence cannot be effective before it is registered (see section 334 for registration).

section.heading: Conditions applicable to works licence on renewal

content.p: If the provisional renewal is properly accepted, the licence is subject to:
the conditions specified in the notice given to the licence holder under section 296; or
if the Joint Authority amended those conditions under section 297—those conditions as amended.

section.heading: Lapse of provisional renewal of works licence

content.p: If the provisional renewal of the licence is not properly accepted under section 300, the provisional renewal lapses.

section.heading: General

content.p: The sources of obligations associated with a works licence are:
the licence conditions; and
obligations arising from compliance directions given by the Designated Authority; and
obligations imposed by this Act and the regulations.
Note: For paragraph (a) see sections 304 and 305. For paragraph (b) see section 387. For paragraph (c) see sections 308 to 310 and section 372.
If a works licence has 2 or more holders, all the holders are jointly and severally bound by the obligations that attach to the licence.

section.heading: Conditions of works licence

content.p: The Joint Authority may grant or renew a works licence subject to whatever conditions the Joint Authority thinks are appropriate.
If the Joint Authority grants or renews a works licence subject to conditions, the conditions must be specified in the licence.
Without limiting subsection (1), the Joint Authority may attach the following kinds of conditions to the grant or renewal of a works licence:
a condition requiring the licence holder to take out insurance as required by the Designated Authority;

a condition requiring the holder to carry out certain work in or in relation to the licence area during the term of the licence, and to comply with directions concerning that work given under section 387;
a condition requiring the holder to lodge a security with the Joint Authority;
a condition requiring the holder to keep specified information;
a condition requiring the holder to give the Joint Authority, on request, specified information;
a condition requiring the holder to take steps to protect the environment of the licence area, including conditions relating to:
protecting wildlife; or
minimising the effect on the environment of the licence area and the area surrounding the licence of activities carried out in the licence area;
a condition requiring the holder to repair any damage to the environment caused by activities in the licence area;
a condition requiring the holder to pay a specified penalty to the Commonwealth if the holder does not comply with a licence condition.
A condition under paragraph (3)(c) must specify:
the amount of the security required; and
the kind of security required; and
the manner and form in which the security is to be lodged.
Without limiting paragraph (3)(c), a condition under that paragraph may require the lodgment of a security in the form of a guarantee and if a guarantee is required the condition may specify:
the kind of person who is to give the guarantee; and
the terms of the guarantee.

section.heading: No conditions requiring payment of money

content.p: Except for a condition requiring the payment of a penalty or lodgment of a security, a licence condition must not require the payment of money to:
the Designated Authority; or
the Joint Authority; or
the Commonwealth.

section.heading: Variation of conditions

content.p: If a works licence holder requests the Designated Authority in writing to vary a licence condition, the Joint Authority may vary the condition.
If a Designated Authority gives:
a direction under section 387; or
an approval, consent or exemption under the regulations;

to a works licence holder, the Joint Authority may vary a licence condition to the extent necessary to avoid inconsistency between the licence conditions and the direction, approval, consent or exemption.
The Joint Authority may vary a licence condition subject to whatever conditions the Joint Authority thinks appropriate.
If the Joint Authority varies a licence condition, the Designated Authority must give the licence holder a written notice that:
informs the holder of the variation; and
specifies the conditions which have been varied; and
specifies any conditions to which the variation is subject.

section.heading: Exemption from or suspension of conditions

content.p: If a works licence holder requests the Designated Authority in writing to:
suspend a licence condition; or
exempt the holder from complying with a licence condition;
the Joint Authority may:
suspend a licence condition; or
exempt the holder from complying with a licence condition.
If a Designated Authority gives:
a direction under section 387; or
an approval, consent or exemption under the regulations;

to a works licence holder, the Joint Authority may suspend a licence condition, or exempt the holder from compliance with a licence condition, to the extent necessary to avoid inconsistency between the licence conditions and the direction, approval, consent or exemption.
The Joint Authority may:
suspend a licence condition; or
exempt the licence holder from complying with a licence condition;
subject to whatever conditions the Joint Authority thinks appropriate.
If the Joint Authority:
suspends a licence condition; or
exempts the licence holder from complying with a licence condition;
the Designated Authority must give the holder a written notice that:
informs the holder of the exemption or suspension; and
specifies the conditions which have been suspended or affected by the exemption; and
specifies any conditions to which the suspension or exemption is subject.
Note: A suspension or exemption of a condition does not take effect until registered (see section 337).

section.heading: Work practices

content.p: If a person who is:
a works licence holder; or
an associate of the holder;
carries out activities in the licence area that are authorised by the licence, the holder or associate must take all reasonable steps:
to ensure that the activities are carried out at a standard that is accepted as reasonable and proper in the mining industry; and
to protect the health, safety and welfare of people engaged in the activities in and about the licence area; and
to maintain in good repair all structures, equipment and other property in the licence area brought there by the person; and
to remove from the licence area any structure, equipment or other property that:
belongs to the person, or is under the person’s control; and
is not being used, or is not going to be used, in connection with the activities.
Penalty: 200 penalty units.

section.heading: Licence holder must keep specified records etc.

content.p: A works licence holder must:
keep whatever records; and
give whatever records to the Designated Authority for inspection; and
make whatever returns;
are necessary to comply with:
the regulations; or
the licence conditions; or
a direction given by the Designated Authority under section 387.
Note: Under section 387 the Designated Authority may direct a person to keep records and to make returns.
Penalty: 100 penalty units.

section.heading: Licence holder must assist inspectors

content.p: A works licence holder must provide an inspector with reasonable facilities and assistance so that the inspector is able to carry out compliance inspections.
Note: See sections 377 to 384 for compliance inspections.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: General

content.p: A works licence expires if:
the term of the licence expires without the licence being renewed; or
the licence holder surrenders the licence; or
the licence is cancelled.
Note: For paragraph (a) see Division 4. For paragraph (b) see section 312. For paragraph (c) see section 313.

section.heading: Voluntary surrender of works licence

content.p: The holder of a works licence may surrender the licence.
Note: The surrender takes effect when it is registered under section 337 (see subsection 337(5)).

section.heading: Cancellation of works licence

content.p: Subject to subsection (5), the Joint Authority may cancel a works licence if the licence holder:
breaches a licence condition; or
contravenes a provision of this Act or the regulations; or
breaches a condition attached to an approval under subsection 365(2).

If the Joint Authority proposes to cancel a works licence under subsection (1), the Designated Authority must give the licence holder a written notice that informs the holder of the proposed cancellation.
The notice must:
specify the reason for the proposed cancellation; and
invite the holder to make submissions in relation to the proposed cancellation; and
specify the day by which submissions should be given to the Joint Authority; and
specify an address where submissions are to be lodged.
The day specified under paragraph (3)(c) must be not less than 60 days after the day on which the notice is given.
The Joint Authority may cancel a works licence only if:
the holder has been given a notice under subsection (2); and
the Joint Authority has considered:
any submission made by the holder; and
any steps taken by the holder to remedy the circumstances that led to the proposal to cancel the licence and to prevent those circumstances from happening again; and
the Joint Authority is satisfied that no special circumstances exist that justify the licence not being cancelled.

section.heading: Obligations of former works licence holders and former associates

content.p: Subject to subsection (2), if:
a person was:
a works licence holder; or
an associate of a works licence holder; and
the licence:
expires; or
is cancelled; or
is surrendered; and
an obligation associated with the licence arising out of:
a licence condition; or
a direction given under section 387 by the Designated Authority in relation to the licence; or
this Act or the regulations;
has not been discharged; and
the person was bound by that obligation when the person was the works licence holder or an associate;
the person remains bound by the obligation until the obligation is discharged.
The Joint Authority may determine that the person is not subject to:
a particular obligation under this section; or
all the person’s remaining obligations under this section.
A determination under subsection (2) is to be in writing.

section.heading: Special purpose consents

content.p: This Part provides for the grant of special purpose consents.
A special purpose consent may be granted over:
a standard block; or
a reserved block; or
a tender block.
A special purpose consent may be granted over a block even if the block is in the licence area of a licence or the consent area of another special purpose consent.
A special purpose consent can only be granted for:
a scientific investigation; or
a reconnaissance survey; or
the collection of only small amounts of minerals.

The exploration of an area is a reconnaissance survey if the exploration is carried out to work out whether the area explored is sufficiently promising to justify more detailed exploration under an exploration licence.

section.heading: Activities authorised by a special purpose consent

content.p: A special purpose consent holder may:
explore for minerals; and
take samples of or recover minerals;
in the consent area for the purposes specified in the consent.
Note 1: Under subsection 23(1) the concept of exploration extends to activities that are directly related to exploration.
Note 2: Under subsection 24(1) the concept of recovery extends to activities that are directly related to the recovery of minerals.
The grant of a consent does not give the consent holder:
any exclusive or proprietary rights over the blocks covered by the consent; or
any option or preference when it comes to the grant of a licence over blocks covered by the consent.

section.heading: Application for a consent

content.p: A person may apply to the Joint Authority for a special purpose consent.

section.heading: How to apply

content.p: The application must:
be made in writing; and
include details of the activities for which consent is being sought; and
specify the blocks for which the consent is being sought; and
be lodged with the Designated Authority.
If the activity involves the collection of only small amounts of minerals (see paragraph 315(4)(c)), the application must also specify:
