the mineral to be recovered; and
the proposed quantity of the mineral to be recovered.

section.heading: Payment of fee

content.p: The applicant must pay the application fee prescribed by the regulations.
The fee must be paid when the application is made.
The Joint Authority may refund any fee paid under subsection (1) but only if it is satisfied that special circumstances exist that justify the refund of the fee.

section.heading: Applicant must obtain agreement of exploration, retention and mining licence holders affected by the application

content.p: Subject to subsection (3), the applicant must obtain the agreement of interested licence holders to the application.
The agreement must be in writing.
The agreement of an interested licence holder is not necessary if:
the application is for a scientific investigation; and
Australia has obligations under international conventions to allow the investigation.
For the purposes of this section, a licence holder is interested if:
the holder holds an exploration, retention or mining licence; and
the block concerned is inside the licence area.

section.heading: Applicant to notify works licence holders affected by the application

content.p: The applicant must notify interested works licence holders of the application.
The notification:
must be given to the interested works licence holders in writing; and
must give details of the special purpose consent applied for; and
must invite the interested works licence holder to give comments to the Designated Authority within 30 days after the day on which the notice was given.
For the purposes of this section, a works licence holder is interested if the block concerned is inside the works licence area.

section.heading: Commonwealth-State offshore area—Designated Authority must refer application to Joint Authority if certain requirements met

content.p: This section applies if the application covers blocks in a Commonwealth-State offshore area.
If the applicant does what is required by sections 318 to 321, the Designated Authority must refer the application to the Joint Authority.
If the applicant does not do what is required by sections 318 to 321, the Designated Authority:
must not refer the application to the Joint Authority; and
must give the applicant written notice that the application has been refused.
The application lapses if a notice is given under subsection (3).

section.heading: Commonwealth-State offshore area—Joint Authority may grant special purpose consent

content.p: If the Designated Authority for a Commonwealth-State offshore area refers the application to the Joint Authority under section 322, the Joint Authority may:
grant a special purpose consent to the applicant; or
refuse the application.

section.heading: External territory offshore area—how application for special purpose consent dealt with

content.p: This section applies if the application covers blocks in an external territory offshore area.
If the applicant does not do what is required by sections 318 to 321, the responsible Commonwealth Minister (as the Joint Authority for that offshore area) must refuse the application.
If the applicant does what is required by sections 318 to 321, the responsible Commonwealth Minister (as the Joint Authority for that offshore area) may:
grant a special purpose consent to the applicant; or
refuse the application.

section.heading: Matters to be specified in the consent

content.p: The consent must specify:
the blocks covered by the consent; and
the activities authorised by the consent; and
the period for which the consent is to have effect; and
the consent conditions.
If the activity involves the collection of only small amounts of minerals (see paragraph 315(4)(c)), the consent must also specify:
the minerals to be collected; and
the quantities to be collected.
The period specified under paragraph (1)(c) is not to be more than 12 months.

section.heading: Duration of consent

content.p: A consent has effect for the period specified under paragraph 325(1)(c).

section.heading: Conditions of consent

content.p: The Joint Authority may grant a special purpose consent subject to whatever conditions the Joint Authority thinks are appropriate.
Without limiting subsection (1), the Joint Authority may impose conditions that relate to:
reports to be provided by the consent holder about activities carried out under the consent; and
environmental matters.

section.heading: Registers to be kept

content.p: Each Designated Authority must keep an offshore mining register.
Note 1: The main matters entered in the register are:

item.p: the grant or renewal of a licence (see sections 333 and 334);
details of instruments that affect a licence (see section 337);
details of instruments that affect an interest in a licence (see sections 338 and 339);
details of interests in a licence that are acquired by devolution (see section 340);
details of caveats (see section 345).

content.p: Note 2: Section 145.4 of the Criminal Code deals with offences in relation to the proper keeping of the register (for example, falsification of documents).
The register for a particular Commonwealth-State offshore area is to be known as the Commonwealth-State Offshore Mining Register for that State.
The register for a particular external territory offshore area is to be known as the External Territory Offshore Mining Register for that external territory.

section.heading: Associated document files to be kept

content.p: Each Designated Authority must keep an associated document file.
In the associated document file are to be kept the documents that the Designated Authority is required to keep under this Part.
Note: The documents kept in the document file are:

item.p: copies of licences (see subsection 333(6));
copies of instruments that affect licences (see subsection 337(4));
copies of transfers of licences (see subsection 338(6));
copies of other dealings in licences (see subsection 339(4));
caveats (see subsection 345(3));
withdrawals of caveats (see subsection 346(2));
consents to dealings given under section 350 (see subsection 350(6));
copies of court orders under section 351.

section.heading: Form of register and document file

content.p: The register is to be kept in the form and manner determined by the Designated Authority.
Without limiting subsection (1), the register may be kept in the form of a computer record.
The document file is to be kept in the form and manner determined by the Designated Authority.

section.heading: Correction of errors in the register

content.p: Subject to subsection (4), the Designated Authority may correct the register if the Designated Authority is satisfied that:
there is an omission of an entry from the register; or
an entry in the register should not have been made; or
there is an error or defect in an entry in the register.
A person may apply to the Designated Authority for correction of the register under subsection (1).
The application:
must be in writing; and
must specify the correction that is being requested.
If:
the Designated Authority intends to correct the register under subsection (1); and
the correction relates to a licence; and
the correction is not to be made in response to an application under subsection (2) by the licence holder;
the Designated Authority must notify the holder that the Designated Authority intends to correct the register.
The notice:
must be in writing; and
must specify the correction the Designated Authority intends to make; and
must invite the holder to make submissions to the Designated Authority about the proposed correction within the period specified in the notice.
The period specified under paragraph (5)(c) is to be at least 14 days after the day on which the notice is given.
If a notice is given under subsection (4):
the Designated Authority is not to correct the register until the period specified in the notice has ended; and
the Designated Authority is to have regard to any submissions made by the licence holder before the end of that period in exercising the power under subsection (1) to correct the register.

section.heading: Inspection of register and documents

content.p: A person may inspect the register and the document file if the person pays the fee prescribed by the regulations.
The Designated Authority must make the register and the document file available for inspection at all convenient times.

division.heading: Matters to be entered in register

content.p: Subdivision A—Licences

section.heading: Licences

content.p: If the provisional grant of a licence is properly accepted, the Designated Authority must register:
the holder’s name; and
if there is more than one licence holder—the share of the licence held by each holder; and
a description of the licence area, including a map or map reference; and
the term of the licence; and
the date of the provisional grant of the licence; and
the date of registration of the licence; and
an address for the service of notices under this Act.
The address registered under paragraph (1)(g) is to be the address specified by the licence holder by notice in writing to the Designated Authority.
If the holder has not given a notice under subsection (2), the address to be registered under paragraph (1)(g) is to be the address specified in the application that the holder made for the licence.
If the Designated Authority registers a licence under subsection (1):
the licence holder must give the licence to the Designated Authority; and
the Designated Authority must endorse the date of registration on the licence.
The Designated Authority may include in the register any other information about the holder or the terms and conditions of the licence that the Designated Authority thinks is appropriate.
The Designated Authority must retain a copy of each licence granted by the Joint Authority.
A licence is taken to be registered as soon as an entry complying with subsection (1) is made in the register.

section.heading: Renewal of licences

content.p: If the Designated Authority is given an application for the renewal of a licence, the Designated Authority must register the fact.
If the provisional renewal of a licence is properly accepted, the Designated Authority must register:
the renewal; and
the term of the renewal; and
the date of the provisional renewal; and
the date of registration of the renewal.
If the Designated Authority registers the renewal of a licence under subsection (2):
the licence holder must give the licence to the Designated Authority; and
the Designated Authority must endorse on the licence:
the term of the renewal; and
the date of registration of the renewal.
If the Joint Authority refuses to renew a licence, the Designated Authority must register the refusal.

section.heading: Extension of exploration licences

content.p: If the Designated Authority receives an application for the extension of the term of an exploration licence, the Designated Authority must register the fact.
If the Joint Authority refuses to extend the term of an exploration licence, the Designated Authority must register the refusal.
Note: The grant of the extension of the term of an exploration licence is registered under subsection 337(1).

section.heading: Expiry of licences

content.p: If a licence expires because:
its term ends; or
a retention licence or mining licence is granted to the licence holder;
the Designated Authority must register the expiry of the licence.
Note: Cancellation is dealt with under section 337.
If the Designated Authority registers the expiry of a licence under subsection (1):
the licence holder must give the licence to the Designated Authority; and
the Designated Authority must endorse the expiry and the date of the expiry on the licence.

section.heading: Variations etc. to licences

content.p: The Designated Authority must register:
the details of any document under this Act that varies, surrenders, cancels or otherwise affects a licence; and
the details of any document that varies or revokes a document referred to in paragraph (a).
Note: The documents referred to in paragraph (a) are:

item.p: suspension of licence rights (see sections 48 (exploration licence), 135 (retention licence) and 195 (mining licence));

amendment of licence conditions between provisional grant and registration (see sections 67 (exploration licence), 148 (retention licence), 211 (mining licence) and 280 (works licence))—these need to be registered at the same time as the grant is registered because if the conditions are amended between provisional grant and registration a replacement licence reflecting the change in conditions is not issued to the provisional holder;
extension of term (see sections 90, 95 and 97 (exploration licence));
surrender of the whole or a part of a licence (see sections 99, 100 and 127 (exploration licence), 158 and 187 (retention licence), 235 and 264 (mining licence) and 312 (works licence));
voluntary surrender—special approval (see section 100 (exploration licence));
mandatory reduction of licence area—special permission (see section 104 (exploration licence));

amendment of licence conditions between provisional renewal and registration (see sections 111 (exploration licence), 170 (retention licence), 247 (mining licence) and 297 (works licence))—these need to be registered at the same time as the renewal because if the licence conditions are amended between provisional renewal and registration a replacement licence reflecting the changed conditions is not issued to the holder;
variation of conditions (see sections 120 (exploration licence), 179 (retention licence), 256 (mining licence) and 306 (works licence));
exemption from or suspension of condition (see sections 121 (exploration licence), 180 (retention licence) and 257 (mining licence) and 307 (works licence));
cancellation (see sections 130 (exploration licence), 189 and 190 (retention licence), 265 (mining licence) and 313 (works licence));
directions (see sections 387 and 392);
security requirements (see section 399);
approvals of transfers (see section 365).

content.p: Paragraph (1)(a) applies to a document that suspends the rights of a holder of a licence.
Details of a document may be registered by registering a summary of the contents of the document.
The Designated Authority must retain the instrument referred to in subsection (1), or a copy of the instrument.
A document referred to in subsection (1):
has no effect until it is registered; and
is taken to be registered as soon as an entry complying with subsection (1) is made in the register.

section.heading: Transfer of licences

content.p: The Designated Authority must register the transfer of a licence or a share in a licence if:
a party to the transfer lodges the instrument of transfer for registration; and
a party to the transfer lodges a copy of the instrument of transfer; and
the transfer has been approved by the Joint Authority; and
the licence is lodged with the Designated Authority for annotation under subsection (5); and
the fee provided for in the Registration Fees Act is paid; and
the fee prescribed by the regulations is paid; and
section 341 (caveats) does not prevent the registration of the transfer.
Note: Paragraph (c): the Joint Authority’s approval is endorsed on the transfer (see subsection 365(3)).
The Designated Authority must also register the date and time of registration of the transfer.

If a document purports to be a transfer of a licence or a share in a licence, the Designated Authority is to register the document under this section without inquiring into or concerning itself with the legal effectiveness of the document.
If an instrument that transfers a licence or a share in a licence is registered, the Designated Authority must register the name of the transferee as a licence holder.
If the Designated Authority registers the transfer of a licence or a share in a licence, the Designated Authority must annotate the licence to show the transferee as a licence holder.
The Designated Authority must keep the copy of the transfer.
The Designated Authority must return the transfer to the person who lodged it.
The Designated Authority must return the annotated licence to the person who lodged it.
The registration of a document under this section does not give the document any greater effect than it would have had apart from this Act.

section.heading: Other dealings in licences

content.p: The Designated Authority must register a document (other than a transfer of a licence or a share in a licence) that creates, transfers, affects or otherwise deals with an interest in a licence if:
a party to the dealing lodges the document for registration; and
a party to the dealing lodges a copy of the document; and
the fee provided for in the Registration Fees Act is paid; and
the fee prescribed by the regulations is paid; and
section 341 (caveats) does not prevent the registration of the dealing.
The Designated Authority must also register the date and time of registration of the dealing.

If a document purports to create, transfer, affect or otherwise deal with an interest in a licence, the Designated Authority is to register the document under this section without inquiring into or concerning itself with the legal effectiveness of the document.
The Designated Authority must keep the copy of the document.
The Designated Authority must return the document to the person who lodged it.
The registration of a document under this section does not give the document any greater effect than it would have had apart from this Act.

section.heading: Devolution of licences

content.p: If:
the rights of a licence holder have devolved to a person by operation of law; and
the person applies to the Designated Authority in writing to be registered as a licence holder; and
the licence is given to the Designated Authority for annotation under subsection (3); and
the person pays the fee prescribed by the regulations; and
the Designated Authority is satisfied that the applicant is entitled to those rights; and
section 341 (caveats) does not prevent the registration of the person as a licence holder;
the Designated Authority must register the person as a licence holder.
If the Designated Authority registers a person as a licence holder under subsection (1), the Designated Authority must also register the date and time of registration.
If the Designated Authority registers a person as a licence holder under subsection (1), the Designated Authority must annotate the licence accordingly.
The Designated Authority must return the annotated licence to the person who gave it to the Designated Authority.
This section applies to 2 or more persons to whom rights have devolved in the same way as it applies to a single person to whom rights have devolved.
Subdivision B—Caveats

section.heading: Effect of a caveat

content.p: If a caveat is in force on a licence, the Designated Authority must not register a dealing in the licence unless:
the Designated Authority is not required to give the caveat holder notice of the particular dealing; or
the caveat holder consents to the registration of the dealing under section 350; or
a court of competent jurisdiction orders the Designated Authority to register the dealing under section 338 or 339 despite the caveat.
Note 1: For dealing see section 4.

Note 2: Once the caveat holder has been given notice of the dealing, the caveat will lapse at the end of 30 days unless the caveat holder consents to the registration of the dealing or gets a court order extending the life of the caveat.

Note 3: The Designated Authority may not be required to give the caveat holder notice of the dealing because the caveat holder is a party to the dealing or because the dealing falls outside the class of dealings that the caveat holder has specified under subsection 343(2) (see subsection 349(6)).
If a caveat is in force on a licence, the Designated Authority must not register a person under section 340 as a licence holder unless:
the caveat holder consents to the registration under section 350; or
a court of competent jurisdiction orders the Designated Authority to register the person under section 340 despite the caveat.

Note: Once the caveat holder has been given notice, the caveat will lapse at the end of 30 days unless the caveat holder consents to the registration or gets a court order extending the life of the caveat.

section.heading: Lodgment of caveats

content.p: A person who claims an interest in or affecting a licence may lodge with the Designated Authority a caveat on the licence.
Without limiting subsection (1), a person may claim an interest in or affecting a licence even if the interest claimed arises under a document that has not been registered under section 338 or 339.

section.heading: Form of caveat

content.p: A caveat must:
be in accordance with the approved form; and
set out:
the full name and address of the person claiming the interest; and
details of the interest claimed; and
be signed by the person claiming the interest; and
specify an address for service of notices within the State or Territory for which the Designated Authority is responsible.
A caveat may specify the particular dealings that the caveat holder wants to be given notice of under section 349.

section.heading: Payment of fee

content.p: The person lodging a caveat must pay the caveat fee that is specified by the regulations.

section.heading: Caveat to be registered

content.p: If:
a caveat is lodged for registration; and
the caveat complies with section 343; and
the person lodging the caveat pays the fee required by section 344;
the Designated Authority must, subject to subsection (4), register the caveat.
The Designated Authority must register the date on which the caveat was lodged.
The Designated Authority must retain the original of the caveat and endorse on it the date on which it was lodged.
Subsection (1) does not apply if:
a court has made an order under subsection 351(2); and
the order requires the court’s consent to the registration of the caveat; and
the court has not consented to the registration of the caveat.

section.heading: Withdrawal of caveat

content.p: A caveat holder may withdraw the caveat at any time by lodging a written withdrawal with the Designated Authority.
The Designated Authority must:
register details of the withdrawal; and
endorse details of the withdrawal on the original of the caveat; and
retain the original of the withdrawal.

section.heading: Form of withdrawal

content.p: A withdrawal of a caveat:
must be in accordance with the approved form; and
must give details of the caveat; and
must be signed by the caveat holder.

section.heading: Duration of caveat

content.p: A caveat on a licence has effect from the time at which it is lodged with the Designated Authority.
A caveat on a licence ceases to have effect if:
a court of competent jurisdiction makes an order for the removal of the caveat under section 351; or
the caveat is withdrawn under section 346; or
the caveat holder is given notice under subsection 349(1), (2) or (3) and 30 days have passed since the caveat holder was given the notice.
Paragraph (2)(c) does not apply if, before the end of the 30 days, the caveat holder consents to the registration of the dealing or to the registration under section 340.
Paragraph (2)(c) does not apply if, before the end of the 30 days:
the caveat holder applies to a court of competent jurisdiction for an order under section 351 that the caveat be extended beyond the period; and
the court makes an order extending the period.
If a court makes an order under paragraph 351(1)(c), the caveat ceases to have effect at the end of the extended period.
Subsection (5) does not apply if, before the end of the extended period, the caveat holder consents to the registration of the dealing under section 350 or to the registration under section 340.

section.heading: Notice to caveat holder

content.p: If:
a transfer of a licence or a share in a licence is lodged with the Designated Authority under section 338; and
a caveat is in force on the licence;
the Designated Authority must, subject to subsection (6), notify the caveat holder that the transfer has been lodged for registration.
If:
a dealing in a licence (other than a transfer of the licence or a share in the licence) is lodged with the Designated Authority under section 339; and
a caveat is in force on the licence;
the Designated Authority must, subject to subsection (6), notify the caveat holder that the dealing has been lodged for registration.
If:
a person applies to the Designated Authority under section 340 to be registered as a licence holder; and
a caveat is in force on the licence;
the Designated Authority must notify the caveat holder that the application has been made.
If:
a licence holder surrenders the licence or surrenders a block or some of the blocks covered by the licence; and
a caveat is in force on the licence;
the Designated Authority must notify the caveat holder of the surrender.
Notification under subsection (1), (2), (3) or (4) must be by registered post or certified mail.
Notice is not to be given under subsection (1) or (2) if:
the caveat holder is a party to the transfer or dealing concerned; or
the caveat holder has specified the class of dealings the caveat holder wants to receive notice of (see subsection 343(2)) and the transfer or dealing falls outside that class.

section.heading: Caveat holder may consent to approval or registration

content.p: If a caveat holder is given notice under subsection 349(1), the caveat holder may consent to the registration of the transfer.
If a caveat holder is given notice under subsection 349(2), the caveat holder may consent to the registration of the dealing.
If a caveat holder is given notice under subsection 349(3), the caveat holder may consent to the registration of the person as a licence holder.
A consent under this section must be in writing and must be lodged with the Designated Authority.
A consent under this section is only effective if it is given within 30 days after the day on which the caveat holder receives the notice concerned.
The Designated Authority must:
register details of the consent; and
endorse details of the consent on the original of the caveat; and
retain the original of the consent.

section.heading: Orders that can be made by a court in relation to caveats

content.p: A court of competent jurisdiction may:
order the removal of a caveat from a licence; or
order the Designated Authority to register a dealing despite a caveat; or
extend the period provided for by paragraph 348(2)(c).
If:
a court makes an order under paragraph (1)(a) or (b) in relation to the licence; and
the court is satisfied that caveats are being used vexatiously to delay the registration of a document;
the court may also make an order that the Designated Authority is not to register any caveats in respect of the licence unless the court has consented to the registration.
An order under subsection (2) may be for an indefinite period or for a specified period.
If an application is made to the court for an order under subsection (2), the Designated Authority becomes a party to the proceedings.
If a court makes an order under this section, the Designated Authority must:
register details of the order; and
retain a copy of the order.

section.heading: Fees for registration

content.p: The Joint Authority is to determine the amount of the fee payable under the Registration Fees Act for registration of any document or fact.
If:
a document creates, transfers, affects or otherwise deals with a licence or an interest in a licence; and
the Designated Authority determines under subsection (1) the amount of the fee payable under the Registration Fees Act on the basis of the information contained in the document; and
the Designated Authority subsequently becomes satisfied that the document does not fully and truly set out:
the consideration for the transaction it relates to; or
all the other facts and circumstances (if any) that affect the amount of the fee payable under the Registration Fees Act in respect of the document;
the Designated Authority may make a fresh determination under subsection (1) of the amount of the fee.

section.heading: Protection from legal actions

content.p: This section applies to:
a Joint Authority; and
a member of a Joint Authority; and
a person acting under the direction or authority of a Joint Authority; and
a Designated Authority; and
a delegate of a Designated Authority; and
a person acting under the direction or authority of a Designated Authority or a delegate of a Designated Authority.
A person to whom this section applies is not liable to an action, suit or proceeding in relation to an act or matter if:
the act or matter is done or omitted to be done in the exercise or purported exercise of a power or authority given by this Part; and
the act or matter is done or omitted to be done in good faith.

section.heading: Appeals

content.p: The Supreme Court, on the application of a person aggrieved by:
the omission of an entry from a register; or
an entry wrongly existing in a register; or
an error or defect in an entry in a register;
may make any order it thinks appropriate directing correction of the register.
In proceedings under subsection (1), the Supreme Court may decide any necessary or expedient question concerning the rectification of the register.
A copy of a Supreme Court order may be served on the Designated Authority concerned.
If the Designated Authority receives a copy of an order under subsection (3), the Designated Authority must amend the register so that the register accords with the order.

section.heading: Appeals against determinations under section 352

content.p: If a person is dissatisfied with a determination by the Designated Authority under section 352, the person may appeal to the Supreme Court against the determination.
Written notice of an appeal under subsection (1) must be given to the Designated Authority concerned.
The Designated Authority may appear before the Supreme Court in a hearing of an appeal under subsection (1).
If the Supreme Court directs the Designated Authority to appear, the Designated Authority must do so.
On hearing an appeal under subsection (1), the Supreme Court may affirm, revoke or amend the determination of the Designated Authority.

section.heading: Supreme Court

content.p: In this Division, Supreme Court means the Supreme Court of, or having jurisdiction in, the State or territory concerned.

section.heading: Evidentiary value of register

content.p: An offshore mining register is admissible in proceedings as prima facie evidence of the matters registered in it.
If the register is kept by the use of a computer, the Designated Authority may issue a document containing the details of a matter taken from the register.
The document issued under subsection (2) is admissible in proceedings as prima facie evidence of the matter.
The Designated Authority may give a person a certified copy of, or extract from, the register if the person pays the fee prescribed by the regulations.
The certified copy is admissible in proceedings without any further proof of, or the production of, the original.

section.heading: Certified copy of document on associated document file

content.p: The Designated Authority may give a person a certified copy of a document that is kept on the associated document file if the person pays the fee prescribed by the regulations.
The certified copy is admissible in proceedings without any further proof of, or the production of, the original.

section.heading: Certification of registration action

content.p: The Designated Authority may give a person a signed certificate that:
a thing required or allowed by this Part has been done; or
a thing required or allowed by this Part has not been done;
if the person pays the fee prescribed by the regulations.
The certificate is admissible in proceedings as prima facie evidence of the facts asserted by the certificate.

division.heading: Dealings in licences to be in writing and registered

section.heading: Dealings in licences to be in writing

content.p: An interest in a licence may be created, transferred, affected or otherwise dealt with only by a written document.
Note: A transfer must be in writing because it is a dealing.
Subsection (1) does not apply to the rights of a licence holder that devolve to a person by operation of law.
Note 1: Rights might devolve to a person, for example, by operation of the laws relating to intestacy or bankruptcy.
Note 2: For the registration of rights that devolve to a person by operation of law see section 340.

section.heading: Dealings in interests in licences not effective until registered

content.p: A document that creates, transfers, affects or otherwise deals with an interest in a licence has no effect until it is registered under Part 3.1.
Note 1: A transfer is a dealing and does not take effect until registered.
Note 2: Transfers are registered under section 338 and other dealings under section 339.

section.heading: Transfers require approval by Joint Authority

content.p: The transfer of a licence has no effect before the transfer is approved by the Joint Authority.
Note 1: For transfer of a licence see subsection 7(1).
Note 2: A transfer is a dealing and under section 361 does not take effect until registered.
The transfer of a share of a licence has no effect before the transfer is approved by the Joint Authority.
Note 1: For transfer of a share of a licence see subsections 7(2) and (3).
Note 2: A transfer is a dealing and under section 361 does not take effect until registered.

section.heading: Application for approval of transfer

content.p: A person may apply to the Joint Authority for approval of the transfer.
The application:
must be in writing; and
must be lodged with the Designated Authority.
The application must be accompanied by:
the transfer document (duly signed or executed); and
a copy of the transfer document; and
if a caveat holder has consented to the registration of the transfer under subsection 350(1)—a copy of the consent.
The application may include a statement of any matter that the applicant wants the Joint Authority to take into account in deciding whether to approve the transfer.
Without limiting subsection (4), the application may include a statement about:
the technical qualifications of a party to the transfer; or
the technical qualifications of the employees of a party to the transfer; or
the technical advice available to a party to the transfer; or
the financial resources of a party to the transfer.
The application must be accompanied by the fee prescribed by the regulations.

section.heading: Designated Authority may ask for further information

content.p: If:
an application is made under section 363 for approval of a transfer; and
the Designated Authority has reason to believe that a person possesses or controls a document that relates to:
the transfer document; or
the transfer transaction; or
the application for approval of the transfer;
the Designated Authority may ask the person:
to give the document to the Designated Authority; or
to make the document available for inspection by or on behalf of:
the Designated Authority; or
the Joint Authority.
The request under subsection (1) must be made by giving to the person a written notice containing the request.
A person must not fail to comply with a request under subsection (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subsection (3) does not apply if the person has a reasonable excuse.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in subsection (4), see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Joint Authority’s response to application for approval

content.p: If an application is made under section 363, the Joint Authority may:
approve the transfer; or
refuse to approve the transfer.
The Joint Authority may, under paragraph (1)(a), approve the transfer on the conditions that it considers necessary or desirable in the public interest.
If the Joint Authority approves the transfer, the Designated Authority must endorse on:
the transfer document; and
a copy of the transfer document;
a record of the approval.
Note: A record of the approval will also be entered in the offshore mining register (see subsection 337(1)).

section.heading: Protection from legal actions

content.p: This section applies to:
a Joint Authority; and
a member of a Joint Authority; and
a person acting under the direction or authority of a Joint Authority; and
a Designated Authority; and
a delegate of a Designated Authority; and
a person acting under the direction or authority of a Designated Authority or a delegate of a Designated Authority.
A person to whom this section applies is not liable to an action, suit or proceeding in relation to an act or matter if:
the act or matter is done or omitted to be done in the exercise or purported exercise of a power or authority given by this Part; and
the act or matter is done or omitted to be done in good faith.

section.heading: Designated Authority may ask person for information

content.p: The Designated Authority may ask a person to give the Authority information if:
the information is relevant to the operation of this Act; and
the Authority has reasonable grounds for believing that the person is able to give the information.
Note: The person must comply with the request (see section 372).
The Designated Authority may ask the person to give the information to:
the Designated Authority; or
an inspector nominated by the Designated Authority.
The request must:
be made by written notice given to the person; and
specify the person to whom the information is to be given; and
specify the period within which the information is to be given.
The information must be given:
in writing; and
before the end of the period specified in the request.
The document containing the information must be signed by:
if the information is given by a body corporate—an authorised officer of the body corporate; or
if the information is provided by an individual—the individual.

section.heading: Power to ask person to appear

content.p: If the Designated Authority has reasonable grounds for believing that a person is able to give information that is relevant to the operation of this Act, the Designated Authority may ask the person to appear personally to:
give the information; and
answer questions about the activity to which the information relates.
Note: The person must comply with the request (see section 372).
The Designated Authority may ask a person to appear before:
the Designated Authority; or
an inspector nominated by the Designated Authority.
The request must:
be made by written notice given to the person; and
specify the activity about which the information is sought or questions will be asked; and
specify the address at which the person is to attend; and
specify the day on which and the time at which the person is to attend; and
indicate whether the appearance is to be before the Designated Authority or before a nominated inspector.

section.heading: Power to examine on oath or affirmation

content.p: If a person appears before the Designated Authority or a nominated inspector, the Designated Authority or the inspector may administer an oath or affirmation to the person.
The oath or affirmation to be administered is an oath or affirmation that the person will truthfully answer the questions put by the Designated Authority or the inspector.

section.heading: Designated Authority may ask for documents

content.p: The Designated Authority may ask a person to give the Designated Authority a document if:
the document is relevant to the operation of this Act; and
the Designated Authority has reasonable grounds for believing that the person is able to give the document.
Note: The person must comply with the request (see section 372).
The Designated Authority may ask the person to give the document to:
the Designated Authority; or
an inspector nominated by the Designated Authority.
The request:
must be made by written notice given to the person; and
must specify the person to whom the document is to be given; and
must specify:
the period within which the document is to be given; or
specify the day on which and the time and place at which the document is to be given; and
may specify whether the original or a copy of the document is to be given.
The regulations may provide for the manner in which the Designated Authority is to deal with the document.
Without limiting subsection (4), the regulations may authorise the Designated Authority or inspector to take a copy of the document.

section.heading: Designated Authority may ask for samples

content.p: The Designated Authority may ask a person to give the Designated Authority a sample taken from the seabed or subsoil in the offshore area if:
the sample is relevant to the operation of this Act; and
the Designated Authority has reasonable grounds for believing that the person is able to give the sample.
Note: The person must comply with the request (see section 372).
The Designated Authority may ask the person to give the sample to:
the Designated Authority; or
an inspector nominated by the Designated Authority.
The request:
must be made by written notice given to the person; and
must specify the person to whom the sample is to be given; and
must specify:
the period within which the sample is to be given; or
the day on which and the time and place at which the sample is to be given.
The regulations may provide for the manner in which the Designated Authority or inspector is to deal with the sample.
Without limiting subsection (4), the regulations may authorise the Designated Authority or inspector to test or analyse the sample.

section.heading: Obligation to comply with request under section 367, 368, 370 or 371

content.p: A person must not fail to comply with a request under section 367, 368, 370 or 371.
Penalty: 100 penalty units.
Subsection (1) does not apply if the person has a reasonable excuse.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in subsection (1A), see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
A person is not excused from complying with the request on the ground that complying with the request might tend to incriminate the person or make the person liable to a penalty.
Note: Section 373 provides immunity for the response to the request.
A person must not give false or misleading information:
in response to a request under section 367 or 368; or
in response to a question asked under subsection 368(1).
Penalty for contravention of this subsection: 100 penalty units.

section.heading: Immunity from use of information etc. given in response to request under section 367, 368, 370 or 371

content.p: If a person gives the Designated Authority information in response to a request under section 367 or 368, the following are not admissible in evidence against the person in any proceedings:
the information given in response to the request;
any information, document or thing obtained as a direct or indirect consequence of the giving of the information.
For the purposes of subsection (1), an answer given in response to a question under paragraph 368(1)(b) is information given in response to a request under section 368.
If a person gives the Designated Authority a document in response to a request under section 370, the following are not admissible in evidence against the person in any proceedings:
the document;
the fact of the production of the document by the person;
any information, document or thing obtained as a direct or indirect consequence of the giving of the document.
If a person gives the Designated Authority a sample in response to a request under section 371, the following are not admissible in evidence against the person in any proceedings:
the sample;
the fact of the production of the sample by the person;
any information, document or thing obtained as a direct or indirect consequence of the giving of the sample.
The immunity provided by subsections (1), (3) and (4) does not apply to proceedings for an offence against subsection 372(3).

section.heading: Restrictions on release of confidential material

content.p: Subject to sections 375 and 376, if the Designated Authority holds confidential information:
the Designated Authority; and
a State or Commonwealth Minister who is given the information under section 375; and
a person who is given the information under subsection 376(3);
must not:
publish the information; or
make the information available to a person.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 2 years.
Subject to section 375, if the Designated Authority holds a confidential sample:
the Designated Authority; and
a Commonwealth or State Minister who is given access to the sample under section 375; and
a person who is given access to the sample under subsection 375(4);
must not:
allow a person to inspect the sample; or
publish information about the sample.
Penalty for contravention of this subsection: Imprisonment for 2 years.

section.heading: Circumstances in which confidential material may be released

content.p: If:
a licence holder gives confidential information to the Designated Authority; and
the holder:
makes the information publicly available; or
consents in writing to the information being made publicly available;
the Designated Authority or a Commonwealth or State Minister who is given access to the information may make the information available to any person.
If:
a licence holder gives a confidential sample to the Designated Authority; and
the holder:
publishes details of the sample; or
consents in writing to the details being made publicly available; or
consents in writing to the sample being made available for public inspection;
the Designated Authority or a Commonwealth or State Minister who is given access to the sample may:
make details of the sample available to any person; or
allow any person to inspect the sample.
Note 1: For confidential information and confidential sample see sections 27 and 28.
Note 2: A Commonwealth or State Minister may be given access to confidential information or a confidential sample under section 416.
Confidential information may be made available to a person if the information is made available for the purposes of the administration of this Act or an associated revenue Act.
A person may be given access to a confidential sample if the access is given for the purposes of the administration of this Act or an associated revenue Act.

section.heading: Certain reports to be made available

content.p: If:
in order to comply with:
the regulations; or
a compliance direction ; or
a licence condition;
a licence holder gives the Designated Authority a report; and
the report relates to blocks that are no longer covered by the licence or by a successor licence to the licence; and
another person requests the Designated Authority to make the report available to the person;
the Designated Authority must make the report available to the person.

section.heading: Compliance inspections

content.p: For the purposes of this Act, a compliance inspection is an inspection carried out to determine whether a licence holder, a special purpose consent holder or an associate has complied with or is complying with:
this Act or the regulations; or
an associated revenue Act or regulations made under an associated revenue Act; or
the licence or consent conditions; or
a compliance direction.
Note 1: For associated revenue Act see section 4.
Note 2: An inspector may carry out a compliance inspection under:

item.p: section 379 (inspection of licence-related premises etc. without a warrant);
section 380 (inspection of other premises etc. with consent of the occupier);
section 381 (inspection of premises etc. with a warrant).

section.heading: Powers exercisable in course of inspection

content.p: If an inspector may carry out a compliance inspection, the inspector may do anything that is reasonable and necessary to carry out the inspection.
Without limiting subsection (1), the inspector may:
examine things that are being used in activities carried out under a licence or special purpose consent and things that appear to the inspector to be intended to be used in those activities; and
test equipment (for example, by operating it); and
examine, and copy, documents; and
remove documents; and
take photographs; and
examine, and take samples of, cores or cuttings from the seabed or subsoil; and
enter or go onto any land, building or structure; and
enter or board any vehicle, vessel or aircraft.
If the compliance inspection is being carried out under a warrant under section 382, subsection (2) has effect subject to the restrictions that are specified in the warrant.

Subject to subsections (5) and (6), if an inspector removes a document under paragraph (2)(d), the inspector may retain the document for as long as is necessary and reasonable to determine whether the licence holder, the consent holder or the associate has complied with or is complying with:
this Act and the regulations; or
an associated revenue Act or regulations made under an associated revenue Act; or
the licence or consent conditions; or
a compliance direction.
Subject to subsection (6), the inspector must not retain the document for more than 60 days.
If:
proceedings for an offence against a provision of this Act or the regulations are instituted within that period of 60 days; and
the document may afford evidence of the commission of the offence;
the inspector may retain the document until the proceedings are completed.
For the purposes of subsection (6):
an offence:
(i) against section 6 of the Crimes Act 1914; or
(ii) that is taken to have been committed because of section 11.2 or 11.2A of the Criminal Code; or
(iii) against section 11.1, 11.4 or 11.5 of the Criminal Code;
that relates to a provision of this Act is taken to be an offence against a provision of this Act; and
an offence:
(i) against section 6 of the Crimes Act 1914; or
(ii) that is taken to have been committed because of section 11.2 or 11.2A of the Criminal Code; or
(iii) against section 11.1, 11.4 or 11.5 of the Criminal Code;
that relates to a provision of the regulations is taken to be an offence against a provision of the regulations; and
the proceedings for an offence are taken to include any appeal to a court in relation to those proceedings.

While an inspector is retaining the document under subsection (4), the inspector must allow a person to inspect the document if the person would have a right to inspect the document if it were not in the inspector’s possession.

section.heading: Inspection of licence-related premises etc. without warrant

content.p: Subject to subsections (2), (3) and (4), an inspector may, without a warrant, carry out a compliance inspection of:
licence-related land; or
a licence-related building, structure, vehicle, vessel or aircraft;
if the inspection is reasonably necessary.
An inspection under subsection (1) must be made at a reasonable time.
An inspector may not enter premises under subsection (1) if:
the premises are a residence; and
the occupier has not consented to the entry.
An inspector may not carry out a compliance inspection under subsection (1) if:
the person occupying or in charge of the land, building, structure, vehicle, vessel or aircraft concerned asks the inspector to produce the inspector’s identity card for inspection by the person; and
the inspector does not comply with the person’s request.
For the purposes of this section, land or a building, structure, vehicle, vessel or aircraft is licence-related if:
it is used in connection with activities carried out under a licence or special purpose consent; or
records about activities of that kind are kept there.

section.heading: Inspection of other premises etc. with occupier’s consent

content.p: An inspector may carry out a compliance inspection of land or a building, structure, vehicle, vessel or aircraft with the consent of the person who occupies or is in charge of the land, building, structure, vehicle, vessel or aircraft.

section.heading: Inspection of other premises etc. with warrant

content.p: An inspector may carry out a compliance inspection in accordance with a warrant issued under section 382.

section.heading: Procedure for obtaining warrant

content.p: An inspector may apply to a magistrate for a warrant to carry out a compliance inspection of land or of a building, structure, vehicle, vessel or aircraft.
The application must be supported by an information on oath or affirmation that sets out the grounds on which the inspector is applying for the warrant.
If the magistrate is satisfied that the compliance inspection is reasonably necessary, the magistrate may issue a warrant to the inspector to carry out the inspection.
The warrant must state:
the name of the inspector; and
whether the inspection may be carried out at any time or only during specified hours of the day; and
the day on which the warrant ceases to have effect; and
the purposes for which the warrant is issued.
The day specified under paragraph (4)(c) is not to be more than 7 days after the day on which the warrant is issued.
The purposes specified under paragraph (4)(d) must include the identification of:
the land, building, structure, vehicle, vessel or aircraft to be inspected; and
any equipment that the inspector may test; and
any documents that the inspector may examine and copy; and
any cores or cuttings from the seabed or subsoil that the inspector may examine and take samples of.

section.heading: Warrant authorises reasonable assistance and force

content.p: If a warrant for a compliance inspection is issued to an inspector under section 382, the warrant authorises the inspector to carry out the inspection:
with such assistance as is reasonable and necessary; and
by such force as is reasonable and necessary.

section.heading: Occupier to cooperate with inspector

content.p: If an inspector carries out a compliance inspection of land or of a building, structure, vehicle, vessel or aircraft under section 379 or 381, the person who occupies or is in charge of it must provide the inspector with the facilities and assistance that the inspector reasonably requires for carrying out the inspection.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Directions by Designated Authority must be obeyed

content.p: A person must not fail to comply with a compliance direction.
Penalty: 100 penalty units.
A person must not fail to comply with a supplementary direction given by the Designated Authority under subsection 391(2).
Penalty for contravention of this subsection: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Scope of compliance directions

content.p: A Designated Authority may give a compliance direction if it is necessary or convenient to do so to carry out or give effect to this Act or the regulations.
Without limiting subsection (1), compliance directions may be given in relation to:
the control of offshore exploration or mining activities; and
the conservation and protection of the mineral resources of offshore areas; and
the remedying of:
damage caused to the seabed or subsoil in an offshore area by offshore exploration or mining activities; or
damage caused by the escape of substances as a result of offshore exploration or mining activities; and
the protection of the environment; and
the keeping of records, cores and samples; and
the giving of records, cores and samples to the Designated Authority for inspection; and
the making of returns.
Note: For offshore exploration or mining activities see section 4.
For the purposes of subsection (2), the control of offshore exploration or mining activities extends to the control of:
the construction, maintenance and operation of installations used in or for use in offshore exploration or mining activities; and
the flow or discharge of fluids arising from offshore exploration or mining activities; and
the safety, health and welfare of people working in offshore exploration or mining activities; and
the maintenance of structures, equipment and property used in or for use in offshore exploration or mining activities.
Note: For offshore exploration or mining activities see section 4.

section.heading: Designated Authority may give directions

content.p: Subject to subsections (2), (3) and (4), the Designated Authority may direct a licence holder or special purpose consent holder to do or not to do the thing specified in the direction.
The direction must be in writing and is given by serving it on the holder.
The Designated Authority must not give a direction of a permanent or standing nature unless the Joint Authority has approved the direction.
Subsection (3) does not apply to the Designated Authority of an external territory offshore area.
Note: The responsible Commonwealth Minister is both the Designated Authority and the Joint Authority for an external territory offshore area.
A failure to comply with subsection (3) does not affect the validity of the direction concerned.

section.heading: Direction may incorporate material in another document

content.p: A direction under section 387 may apply, adopt or incorporate a code of practice or a standard that is contained in another document.
The application, adoption or incorporation of the other document may be made with or without modification.
The other document may be one issued outside Australia.
The direction may apply, adopt or modify the other document:
as in force at the time when the direction is given; or
as in force from time to time.

If a direction applies, adopts or incorporates material in another document, a copy of the document must be attached to the direction when it is given to the licence holder or special purpose consent holder.

section.heading: Direction may impose absolute prohibition

content.p: Without limiting section 387:
a direction may prohibit absolutely the doing of a thing; and
a direction may prohibit the doing of a thing unless a person’s consent or approval is obtained.

section.heading: Compliance direction may extend to associates

content.p: A compliance direction to a licence holder or special purpose consent holder may extend to an associate specified in the direction.
The direction may provide that only particular obligations specified in the direction extend to a particular associate.
Note: An associate may be specified by name or as a member of a class of associates (see subsection 33(3AB) of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901).

section.heading: Holder to give notice of direction to associates

content.p: If a direction under section 387 extends to an associate, the licence holder or special purpose consent holder must either:
give a copy of the direction to the associate; or
display a copy of the direction at a place that the associate goes to in the course of carrying out activities under the licence or consent.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The Designated Authority may give the licence holder or special purpose consent holder a supplementary direction that specifies:
the manner in which copies of a direction are to be displayed under paragraph (1)(b); or
the places at which copies of a direction are to be displayed under paragraph (1)(b).

section.heading: Power to give directions after licence etc. ends

content.p: If a person is bound by an obligation because of section 131, 191, 266 or 314, the Designated Authority may direct the person to do a thing or not to do a thing specified in the direction.
A direction may be given only for the following purposes:
to ensure that the obligation is complied with;
a purpose that is incidental to the purpose in paragraph (a).
Note: Sections 131, 191, 266 and 314 provide for undischarged obligations to continue to bind a former licence holder or associate after the licence ends.
A direction must be in writing and is given by serving it on the person bound by the obligation.

section.heading: Effect of a compliance direction on other instruments

content.p: A later compliance direction overrides an earlier compliance direction if they are inconsistent.
A compliance direction has effect despite anything in:
the regulations; or
a State offshore law that is applied to an offshore area by section 428; or
a licence condition that relates to safety or environmental matters.

section.heading: Designated Authority may specify time for compliance

content.p: If the Designated Authority gives compliance direction to a licence holder or special purpose consent holder, the Designated Authority may:
specify in the direction a time for compliance with the direction; or
give the holder a supplementary direction under this section specifying a time for compliance with the direction.

section.heading: Designated Authority may take action if holder fails to comply

content.p: The Designated Authority may do all or any of the things required by a compliance direction if:
the time for compliance specified under section 394 has ended; and
the person to whom the direction was given or to whom it extended has not complied with the direction.
The Designated Authority must not take action under subsection (1) without the Joint Authority’s approval if the direction required that approval.

section.heading: Costs incurred by Designated Authority in taking action under section 395

content.p: If:
the Designated Authority takes action under section 395 in relation to a compliance direction given to a licence holder or special purpose consent holder; and
the direction does not extend to an associate of the holder;
the costs and expenses incurred by the Designated Authority in taking that action are a debt due to the Commonwealth by the holder.
If:
a compliance direction specifies that a particular associate of a licence holder or special purpose consent holder is subject to a particular obligation; and
the Designated Authority takes action under section 395 in relation to that obligation;
the costs and expenses incurred by the Designated Authority in taking that action are a debt due to the Commonwealth by the holder and the associate.
The associate and the holder are jointly and severally liable to pay the debt arising under subsection (2).
A debt under this section is recoverable in a court of competent jurisdiction.

section.heading: Defences to actions to recover debts

content.p: It is a defence to an action to recover the debt from the licence holder or special purpose consent holder if:
the holder produces evidence that the holder took all reasonable steps to comply with the compliance direction; and
the evidence is not rebutted.
It is a defence to an action to recover the debt from the associate if:
the associate produces evidence that the associate did not know of, and could not reasonably be expected to know of, the existence of the compliance direction; and
the evidence is not rebutted.

section.heading: Securities

content.p: A person may be required to lodge a security with the Designated Authority under:
section 399 (security as prerequisite for proper acceptance of provisional grant or provisional renewal); or
section 118 (exploration licence conditions), 177 (retention licence conditions), 254 (mining licence conditions) or 304 (works licence conditions).
Securities are required as a way of ensuring compliance with this Act and with licence conditions. Securities may only be used for the purposes laid down in section 400.

section.heading: Determination of requirement to lodge security

content.p: The Joint Authority may determine that a person who has been provisionally granted a licence must lodge a security with the Designated Authority.
Note 1: The provisional holder will be given notice of the determination under section 66 or 83 (exploration licence), 147 (retention licence), 210 or 227 (mining licence) or 279 (works licence).

Note 2: If the provisional holder does not lodge the security within a particular time provided for in this Act, the provisional grant will lapse (see section 72 or 86 (exploration licence), 153 (retention licence), 216 or 230 (mining licence) or 285 (works licence)).
If the Joint Authority provisionally renews a licence, the Joint Authority may determine that the licence holder must lodge a security with the Designated Authority.
Note 1: The licence holder will be given notice of the determination under section 110 (exploration licence), 169 (retention licence), 246 (mining licence) or 296 (works licence).

Note 2: If the holder does not lodge the security within a particular time provided for in this Act, the provisional renewal will lapse (see section 116 (exploration licence), 175 (retention licence), 252 (mining licence) or 302 (works licence)).
A determination under subsection (1) or (2) must specify:
the amount of the security required; and
the kind of security required; and
the manner and form in which the security is to be lodged.
Without limiting subsections (1) and (2), a determination may require the lodgment of a security in the form of a guarantee and if a guarantee is required the determination may specify:
the kind of person who is to give the guarantee; and
the terms of the guarantee.
The determination is to be in writing.

If the person is provisionally granted a licence over a tender block, the amount determined as a security under subsection (1) is to be the amount of security referred to in the tender block licence notice.

section.heading: Application of security

content.p: If:
a person is a licence holder; and
the person has lodged a security with the Designated Authority;
the Joint Authority may use the security to discharge the person’s obligations arising from a failure to comply with:
this Act; or
the licence conditions; or
a compliance direction.
Without limiting subsection (1), the holder’s financial obligations include the obligation to pay a penalty imposed under the licence conditions.
Subject to subsection (1), the Joint Authority is to deal with a security in accordance with the regulations.

section.heading: Removal of property from offshore area

content.p: The regulations may provide for:
the removal from an offshore area of property that:
has been brought into the offshore area for use in offshore exploration or mining activities; and
is not being used and is not intended to be used in exploration or mining activities in accordance with a licence; and
the disposal by the Designated Authority of property removed under regulations made for the purposes of paragraph (a); and
the recovery of costs and expenses incurred by the Designated Authority in removing or disposing of property in accordance with regulations made for the purposes of paragraphs (a) and (b).
Regulations made for the purposes of paragraph (1)(a) may provide for removal by the Designated Authority or by someone else.
Regulations made for the purposes of paragraph (1)(c) may provide for the recovery of costs by way of deduction from the proceeds of the disposal.
Subject to the regulations, no action lies in respect of the removal or disposal of property in accordance with the regulations.
In this section:
property includes a structure or equipment.

section.heading: Rehabilitation of damaged areas

content.p: The regulations may provide for:
the rehabilitation of an area in an offshore area that has been damaged or affected by exploration or mining activities of a licence holder; and
the recovery of costs and expenses incurred by the Designated Authority in rehabilitating an area under regulations made for the purposes of paragraph (a).
Regulations made for the purposes of paragraph (1)(a) may provide for the rehabilitation to be carried out by the Designated Authority or someone else.
Regulations made for the purposes of paragraph (1)(a) may provide for the recovery of costs and expenses by way of deduction from the licence holder’s security.

section.heading: Declaration of safety zone around a structure or equipment

content.p: The Designated Authority may declare a safety zone around a structure or equipment in an offshore area.
A declaration may only be made for the purpose of protecting the structure or equipment.
The safety zone may extend not more than 500 metres from the outer edge of the structure or equipment.
The declaration is to be made by notice published in the Gazette.
The declaration may apply to:
all vessels; or
all vessels except those specified in the declaration.

section.heading: Effect of declaration of safety zone

content.p: If a safety zone is declared around a structure or equipment, a vessel to which the declaration applies is not to enter or remain in the safety zone without the written consent of the Designated Authority.
If:
a safety zone is declared around a structure or equipment; and
the Designated Authority consents to a vessel entering or remaining in the safety zone; and
the consent is given on conditions;
the vessel is to enter or remain in the safety zone only in accordance with the conditions.

The owner of a vessel and the person in command or in charge of a vessel each commit an offence against this section if the vessel enters or remains in a safety zone in contravention of subsection (1) or (2).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 5 years.
It is a defence to a prosecution of a person for an offence against subsection (3) if the person satisfies the court that:
an unforeseen emergency made it necessary for the vessel to enter or remain in the safety zone to attempt to secure the safety of:
a human life; or
the vessel; or
another vessel; or
a well, pipeline, structure or equipment; or
the vessel entered or remained in the safety zone in circumstances beyond the control of the person who was in command or in charge of the vessel (for example, adverse weather).
Note: The defendant bears a legal burden in relation to the matter in subsection (4), see section 13.4 of the Criminal Code.

An owner is not criminally responsible for an offence against subsection (3) if the owner proves that the owner did not know that the person in command or in charge of the vessel was in contravention of subsection (3).
Note: The defendant bears a legal burden in relation to the matter in subsection (5), see section 13.4 of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: General regime for criminal offences

content.p: The following provisions of this Act create offences:
section 38 (exploration or recovery without appropriate authorisation);
section 44 (interference with rights);
sections 123, 183, 259 and 308 (failure to comply with work practice requirements);
sections 124, 184, 261 and 309 (failure to keep records);
sections 125, 185, 262, 310 and 384 (failure to assist inspector);
section 364 (failure to give document relevant to application for approval of a transfer);
section 372 (failure to appear or to provide information, document or samples);
section 374 (failure to keep information etc. confidential);
section 385 (failure to comply with a direction given by Designated Authority);
subsection 391(1) (failure to give associate notice of a direction);
section 404 (failure to comply with safety zone conditions);
section 423 (failure to return an inspector identity card).
(2) The Crimes Act 1914 and the Criminal Code contain provisions that are relevant to the operation of this Act.
Note 1: See sections 4AA, 4AB and 4B of the Crimes Act 1914 for further details on penalties. Section 4AA provides for the amount of a penalty unit.

Note 2: See Parts 7.3 and 7.4 of the Criminal Code (which deal with fraudulent conduct and false or misleading statements). Those Parts are relevant to statements made in applications under this Act and statements made in documents that are relevant to the calculation of fees (for example, fees payable under the Registration Fees Act for transfers and other dealings).
Note 3: See Part 5.6 of the Criminal Code for offences relating to secrecy of information.

Note 4: See section 145.4 of the Criminal Code for a general offence relating to the falsification of documents kept for the purposes of a law of the Commonwealth. This offence is relevant to offshore mining registers.
Note 5: See also the following provisions of the Crimes Act 1914:

item.p: section 4J (when indictable offences can be dealt with summarily);
section 4K (continuing offences);
section 15B (time for bringing prosecutions);
section 35 (giving false testimony).

content.p: Note 6: The Proceeds of Crimes Act 1987 provides for pecuniary penalties and forfeiture orders.
Note 7: See also section 149.1 of the Criminal Code, which deals with obstruction of Commonwealth public officials.

part.heading: Review of decisions made about the offshore areas of external territories

section.heading: Definitions

content.p: In this Part:
application period means:
the period of 30 days from the day on which the applicant is given notice of the decision; or
if the Designated Authority extends the application period under subsection 407(3)—the extended period.
decision has the same meaning as it has in the Administrative Review Tribunal Act 2024.
Designated Authority means the responsible Commonwealth Minister acting as Designated Authority for an external territory offshore area.
reviewable decision means a decision made by the Designated Authority (including a decision made under subsection 407(3)).
reviewable delegated decision means a decision made by a delegate of the Designated Authority under section 419.

section.heading: Review of delegated decisions

content.p: A person whose interests are affected by a reviewable delegated decision may apply to the Designated Authority for reconsideration of the decision.
An application under subsection (1) must:
be in writing; and
be given to the Designated Authority before the end of the application period; and
set out the applicant’s reasons for seeking a review of the decision.
The Designated Authority may extend the application period if the applicant asks for an extension before the end of the period.
The Designated Authority must reconsider a reviewable delegated decision as soon as possible after receiving an application under subsection (1).
The Designated Authority may:
confirm the reviewable delegated decision; or
revoke the decision; or
revoke the decision and make a new decision instead of the revoked decision.
The Designated Authority must give the applicant a written notice that informs the applicant:
of the outcome of the reconsideration; and
that the applicant may apply to the Administrative Review Tribunal for review of the reconsideration; and
(c) that the applicant may request a statement of reasons in relation to the reconsideration under the Administrative Review Tribunal Act 2024.

If an applicant is not given notice of the result of the reconsideration within 60 days after the day on which the applicant lodged the application, the Designated Authority is taken to have confirmed the reviewable delegated decision.
Failure to comply with the requirements of subsection (6) in relation to a reviewable delegated decision does not affect the validity of the decision.
A person whose interests are affected by a reviewable decision may apply to the Administrative Review Tribunal for review of the decision.

part.heading: Procedures of Joint Authorities and Designated Authorities

section.heading: Procedure of Joint Authority

content.p: A Joint Authority may conduct its business:
at meetings of the Authority; or
by written or other communication between the members of the Authority.

section.heading: Decision-making

content.p: This section applies to decisions to be made by a Joint Authority on matters that are within the Authority’s functions.

If the responsible Commonwealth Minister and the responsible State Minister disagree about a decision, the responsible Commonwealth Minister may decide the matter and the responsible Commonwealth Minister’s decision has effect as the Authority’s decision.
If:
the responsible Commonwealth Minister gives the responsible State Minister written notice of a decision that the responsible Commonwealth Minister thinks should be made on a matter; and
the responsible State Minister has not told the responsible Commonwealth Minister what decision the responsible State Minister thinks should be made within 30 days after the notice is given;
the responsible Commonwealth Minister may decide the matter and his or her decision has effect as the Authority’s decision.

section.heading: Opinion or state of mind of Joint Authority

content.p: For the purposes of this Act, the opinion or state of mind of the Joint Authority is:
if the responsible Commonwealth Minister and the responsible State Minister agree on the matter concerned—the opinion or state of mind of the 2 Ministers; or
if the 2 Ministers do not agree—the opinion or state of mind of the responsible Commonwealth Minister.

section.heading: Records of proceedings of Joint Authority

content.p: The Designated Authority is to keep written records of the decisions of the Joint Authority.

A record kept under subsection (1) is prima facie evidence that the decision was duly made as recorded if the record is signed by a person who was a member of the Joint Authority at the time when the decision was made.

section.heading: Signing of documents

content.p: If a document is signed by the Designated Authority on behalf of the Joint Authority, the document is taken to have been duly executed by the Joint Authority.
The document is taken to be in accordance with a decision of the Joint Authority unless the contrary is proved.

section.heading: Communications with Joint Authority

content.p: All communications to or by the Joint Authority are to be made through the Designated Authority.

section.heading: Ministerial colleague acting on behalf of responsible Commonwealth Minister

content.p: Another Commonwealth Minister may act for and on behalf of the responsible Commonwealth Minister for the purposes of this Act.

section.heading: Acting responsible Commonwealth Minister

content.p: The functions and powers of the responsible Commonwealth Minister under this Act may be performed and exercised by another Commonwealth Minister acting for and on behalf of the responsible Commonwealth Minister.
The functions and powers referred to in subsection (1) include functions and powers that the responsible Commonwealth Minister has as a member of a Joint Authority.

section.heading: Circumstances in which confidential material released

content.p: If:
the Designated Authority holds confidential information or a confidential sample; and
the responsible Commonwealth Minister seeks access to the information or sample;
the Designated Authority must make the information or sample available to the Minister.
Note: This subsection cannot apply to the Designated Authority of an external territory offshore area because the responsible Commonwealth Minister is the Designated Authority.
If:
the Designated Authority holds any document:
associated with confidential information or a confidential sample; and
received or issued by the Designated Authority for the purposes of this Act; and
the responsible Commonwealth Minister seeks access to the document;
the Designated Authority must make the document available to the Minister.
Note: This subsection cannot apply to the Designated Authority of an external territory offshore area because the responsible Commonwealth Minister is the Designated Authority.
If:
the Designated Authority holds any document:
associated with confidential information or a confidential sample; and
that is a copy of a notice or direction issued by the Designated Authority for the purposes of this Act; and
the responsible Commonwealth Minister seeks access to the document;
the Designated Authority must make the document available to the Minister.
