Note: This subsection cannot apply to the Designated Authority of an external territory offshore area because the responsible Commonwealth Minister is the Designated Authority.
The Designated Authority may make confidential information or a confidential sample held by the Designated Authority available to:
a State Minister; or
a Commonwealth Minister.
Note: For confidential information and confidential sample see sections 27 and 28.

section.heading: Execution and issue of documents on behalf of Joint Authority

content.p: If this Act requires or allows a Joint Authority to execute or issue a document, the Designated Authority is to execute or issue the document.

For the purposes of any proceedings, a document that purports to be executed or issued by the Designated Authority is taken to have been executed or issued in accordance with a decision of the Joint Authority unless the contrary is proved.

section.heading: Service of notices on behalf of Joint Authority

content.p: If this Act requires or allows a Joint Authority to:
give a notice; or
communicate a matter;
the Designated Authority is to give the notice or communicate the matter.

For the purposes of any proceedings, a notice that purports to be given by the Designated Authority is taken to have been given in accordance with a decision of the Joint Authority unless the contrary is proved.

For the purposes of any proceedings, a communication that purports to be made by the Designated Authority is taken to have been made in accordance with a decision of the Joint Authority unless the contrary is proved.

section.heading: Delegation by Designated Authority

content.p: A Designated Authority may by signed instrument delegate to a person all or any of the powers or functions of the Designated Authority under:
this Act; or
an associated revenue Act; or
regulations made under this Act.
Note 1: See also section 34AB of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901.
Note 2: For associated revenue Act see section 4.
A delegation under this section may be made to the person who holds, or performs the duties of, a specified office under the Commonwealth or a State.
If a Designated Authority delegates a power or function under this section, the delegation continues in force despite:
a vacancy in the office of Designated Authority; or
a change in the identity of the holder of the office of Designated Authority.
Despite subsection (3), a delegation under this section may be revoked by a Designated Authority.
A copy of each instrument making, varying or revoking a delegation under this section must be published in the Gazette.

section.heading: Application of this Part to external territories

content.p: Sections 408, 409, 410, 411, 412, 413, 417 and 418 do not apply to the Joint Authority for an external territory.

section.heading: Appointment of inspectors

content.p: The Joint Authority may appoint inspectors for the purposes of this Act and the regulations.
Note: Inspectors have powers under sections 367, 368, 369, 370, 371, 378, 379, 380 and 381.
The appointment must be in writing.

section.heading: Identity cards

content.p: The Designated Authority must issue an inspector with an identity card.
The card must:
contain a recent photograph of the inspector; and
be in the form approved by the Designated Authority.

section.heading: Return of identity card

content.p: A person who stops being an inspector must return his or her identity card to the Designated Authority as soon as practicable.
Penalty: One penalty unit.
Subsection (1) does not apply if the person has a reasonable excuse.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in subsection (2), see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Fees received on behalf of the Commonwealth

content.p: Money received by the Designated Authority as fees payable under this Act is taken to be received by the Designated Authority on behalf of the Commonwealth.

section.heading: Payments by the Commonwealth to the States—Royalty Act payments

content.p: The Commonwealth must pay to each State 60% of royalties payable under the Royalty Act in respect of minerals in the Commonwealth-State offshore area for that State.
Payments under subsection (1) are to be made not later than the end of the month that follows the month in which the royalties concerned were received by the Commonwealth.
In this section:
royalty includes any penalty for late payment of royalty.

section.heading: Payments by the Commonwealth to the States—other payments

content.p: The Commonwealth must pay each State amounts equal to all money that is payable to the Designated Authority for the Commonwealth-State offshore area for that State on behalf of the Commonwealth:
under this Act; or
under an associated revenue Act other than the Royalty Act.
Note: For associated revenue Act see section 4.
Payments under subsection (1) are to be made in accordance with arrangements approved by the responsible Commonwealth Minister.

section.heading: Appropriation

content.p: The Consolidated Revenue Fund is appropriated to the extent necessary for the purposes of sections 425 and 426.

section.heading: State’s or external territory’s offshore laws apply to mineral exploration and recovery in offshore area

content.p: The laws in force in a State apply to offshore exploration and mining activities in the Commonwealth-State offshore area for that State.
An external territory’s laws apply to offshore exploration and mining activities in the external territory offshore area for that territory.
Subsections (1) and (2) apply subject to:
sections 429 to 434 (inclusive); and
regulations made for the purposes of subsection (5).
For the purposes of subsections (1) and (2):
an external territory’s laws are the laws (other than laws of the Commonwealth) that are in force in the external territory; and
laws include unwritten laws (the common law); and
laws include instruments that have effect under laws as defined in paragraphs (a) and (b).
The regulations may provide that a law:
does not apply under subsection (1) in an offshore area; or
applies under subsection (1) in an offshore area with the modifications that are specified in the regulations.
(6) For the purposes of subsection (5), modifications includes additions, omissions and substitutions.

(7) For the purposes of this section, offshore exploration and mining activities includes all acts, omissions, matters, circumstances and things that arise out of or are otherwise connected with those activities.

section.heading: Criminal laws not applied

content.p: (1) Section 428 does not apply to laws that are substantive criminal laws, or laws of criminal investigation, procedure and evidence, within the meaning of Schedule 1 to the Crimes at Sea Act 2000.
(2) Subsection (1) does not detract from the operation of the Crimes at Sea Act 2000.

section.heading: Laws inconsistent with Commonwealth laws not applied

content.p: Section 428 does not apply to a law to the extent that the law would be inconsistent with a law of the Commonwealth.

section.heading: Tax laws not applied

content.p: Section 428 does not apply to a law that imposes a tax.

section.heading: Applied laws not to confer Commonwealth judicial power

content.p: Section 428 does not apply to a State law to the extent to which it would confer judicial power of the Commonwealth on a court, tribunal, authority or officer of a State or external territory.

section.heading: Applied laws not to contravene constitutional restrictions on conferring powers on courts

content.p: Section 428 does not apply to a State law to the extent that it would confer on a State court a power that cannot, under the Constitution, be conferred by the Parliament on such a court.

section.heading: Applied laws not to appropriate Territory Consolidated Revenue Fund

content.p: Section 428 does not apply to a law of an external territory so as to appropriate the public moneys of the territory.

section.heading: Jurisdiction of State courts

content.p: Subject to subsections (2) and (4), a State’s courts are invested with federal jurisdiction in all matters arising under the laws of the State applied under section 428.
Jurisdiction is invested under subsection (1) within the limits (other than limits of locality) of the jurisdiction of the court.
Subsection (2) applies to limits as to subject matter or other limits.
The regulations may provide that subsection (1) does not apply to the jurisdiction of a particular court.
For the purposes of this section, the Northern Territory is not to be treated as though it were a State.

section.heading: Jurisdiction of Territory courts

content.p: Jurisdiction is conferred on the courts that have jurisdiction in a Territory in all matters arising under the laws of the Territory applied under section 428.
Jurisdiction is conferred under subsection (1) within the limits (other than limits of locality) of the jurisdiction of the court.
Subsection (2) applies to limits as to subject matter or other limits.
For the purposes of this section, the Territories are:
the Northern Territory; and
the external territories to which this Act extends under section 36.

section.heading: Validation of certain actions

content.p: If:
a person or a court does an act in the purported exercise of a power or performance of a function under State or external territory law; and
the act could have been done by the person or court in the exercise of a power or performance of a function under the State or territory laws applied under section 428;
the act is taken to have been done in the exercise of the power or function under the applied law.

section.heading: Service of documents on licence holders etc.

content.p: A document that is to be given to a licence holder may be given to the holder by posting it to the address that is the holder’s registered address for service.
Note: See section 333 for registration of an address for service.
A document that is to be given to an applicant for a licence may be given to the applicant by posting it to the address that the applicant specified in the applicant’s application for the licence.

section.heading: Vesting jurisdiction in State courts

content.p: Subject to subsection (4), the several courts of a State are invested with federal jurisdiction with respect to matters arising under:
this Act; and
the associated revenue Acts; and
the regulations.
Subject to subsection (4), jurisdiction is conferred on the several courts of a Territory with respect to matters arising under:
this Act; and
the associated revenue Acts; and
the regulations.
Note: For associated revenue Act see section 4.
Subsections (1) and (2) do not apply to matters that arise under the provisions that are applied under Part 5.1.
Jurisdiction is invested or conferred under subsection (1) or (2) within the limits (other than limits of locality) of the jurisdiction of the court.
Subsection (4) applies to limits as to subject matter or other limits.
For the purposes of this section:
the Northern Territory is not to be treated as though it were a State; and
the Territories are:
the Northern Territory; and
the external territories to which this Act extends under section 36.

section.heading: Licences, and interests in licences etc., are not personal property for the purposes of the Personal Property Securities Act 2009

content.p: Each of the following is declared not to be personal property for the purposes of the Personal Property Securities Act 2009:
a licence;
an interest or right in, or in relation to, a licence.
Note: See paragraph 8(1)(k) of the Personal Property Securities Act 2009.

section.heading: Regulations

content.p: The Governor-General may make regulations prescribing all matters:
required or permitted by this Act to be prescribed; or
necessary or convenient to be prescribed for carrying out or giving effect to this Act.
Without limiting subsection (1), the regulations may provide for:
the control of offshore exploration and mining activities; and
procedures for giving notice to people whose interests might be affected by the grant of a licence; and
the conservation and protection of the mineral resources of offshore areas; and
the remedying of:
damage caused to the seabed or subsoil in an offshore area by offshore exploration and mining activities; or
damage caused by the escape of substances as a result of offshore exploration and mining activities; and
the protection of the environment; and
the keeping of records, cores or samples; and
the giving of records, cores or samples to a Designated Authority for inspection; and
the making of returns; and
the imposition and recovery of fees in respect of access to reports under section 376.
Note: For offshore exploration or mining activities see section 4.
For the purposes of subsection (2), the control of offshore exploration and mining activities extends to the control of:
the construction, maintenance and operation of installations used in or for use in offshore exploration and mining activities; and
the flow or discharge of fluids arising from offshore exploration and mining activities; and
the safety, health and welfare of people working in offshore exploration and mining activities; and
the maintenance of structures, equipment and property used in or for use in offshore exploration and mining activities.
Note: For offshore exploration or mining activities see section 4.
For the purposes of paragraph (2)(b), interests that might be affected by the grant of a licence include native title rights and interests that might be affected by the grant of the licence.
The regulations may provide for offences against the regulations.
The penalties imposed in respect of offences against the regulations are not to exceed:
a fine of 10 penalty units; or
a fine of 10 penalty units for each day on which the offence is taken to continue.
In this section:
control includes restrict.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Correspondence of permits etc. under 1981 Act and licences under this Act

content.p: For the purposes of this Schedule:
an exploration permit under the 1981 Act and an exploration licence under this Act correspond to each other; and
a production licence under the 1981 Act and a mining licence under this Act correspond to each other; and
a works authority under the 1981 Act and a works licence under this Act correspond to each other; and
an instrument of consent under section 74 of the 1981 Act and a special purpose consent under this Act correspond to each other.
If one provision of the 1981 Act and one provision of this Act have the same legal effect, the 2 provisions correspond to each other.
If:
one provision of the 1981 Act has a particular legal effect in relation to a number of permit types; and
a provision of this Act has that legal effect in relation to one only of those permit types;
the 2 provisions correspond to each other for the purposes of applying this Schedule to that permit type.
In this section:
legal effect includes conferring the power to issue a document.
permit type means:
in relation to the 1981 Act:
an exploration permit; or
a production licence; or
a works authority; or
an instrument of consent under section 74 of that Act; and
in relation to this Act:
a retention licence; or
an exploration licence; or
a mining licence; or
a works licence; or
a special purpose consent.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: References in documents to provisions of the 1981 Act

content.p: A reference in a document to a provision of the 1981 Act is to be construed as a reference to the corresponding provision of this Act.

hcontainer.name: part
hcontainer.heading: Savings and transitional provisions applicable on the transition from the Minerals (Submerged Lands) Act 1981 to this Act

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Instruments in force under the 1981 Act on the commencement of this Act

content.p: An instrument that was in force under a provision of the 1981 Act immediately before the commencement of this Act has effect, from that commencement, as if it were an instrument made under the corresponding provision of this Act.
Without limiting subsection (1), the instrument may be:
a determination; or
a direction; or
an approval; or
a notice; or
a declaration.
Subsection (1) does not apply to a delegation under section 20 of the 1981 Act.

If an instrument to which subsection (1) applies was, when made, to have effect only for a limited period, the instrument has effect under subsection (1) only for so much of the period as had not already expired before the commencement of this Act.
Subject to subsection (3), any regulations made under the 1981 Act and in force immediately before the commencement of this Act continue in force as if they were made under this Act.
A reference in a regulation so continued in force to a provision of the 1981 Act is taken to be a reference to the corresponding provision of this Act.
This section does not apply to a regulation the making of which would not be authorised by this Act.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Saving of application for permit etc. under the 1981 Act

content.p: If:
a person applied for an exploration permit under the 1981 Act before the commencement of this Act; and
the application is not determined before that commencement;
the application has effect from that commencement as if it were an application for an exploration licence under this Act.
If:
a person applied for a production licence under the 1981 Act before the commencement of this Act; and
the application is not determined before that commencement;
the application has effect from that commencement as if it were an application for a mining licence under this Act.
If:
a person applied for a works authority under the 1981 Act before the commencement of this Act; and
the application is not determined before that commencement;
the application has effect from that commencement as if it were an application for a works licence under this Act.
If:
a person applied for a consent under section 74 of the 1981 Act before the commencement of this Act; and
the application is not determined before that commencement;
the application has effect from that commencement as if it were an application for a special purpose consent under this Act.

An exploration permit that was in force under the 1981 Act immediately before the commencement of this Act has effect from that commencement as if it were an exploration licence in force under this Act.
If subsection (1) applies to an exploration licence:
the licence remains in force for a period of 2 years commencing on the day on which the licence is granted; and
section 104 of this Act does not apply to the licence.
If:
subsection (1) applies to an exploration licence; and
the licence holder applies to renew the licence;
the holder must surrender on each surrender day of the licence:
25% of the number of blocks in the licence area; or
if 25% of that number is a whole number and a fraction—the next higher whole number.
